title: PV stage-1 fit slices history into 24 h blocks from the tick time, not local days: performance ratio and fan change with the time of day
label: bug
steps: Scratch company; write 15 local days of 5-minute pv_power_w for a 100 kWp/100 kW plant at 31.5N 74.3E equal to solar.pv_power(clear sky) x 1.0 on even local days and x 0.45 on odd days. Call forecast.pv(site, t0) with t0 = local midnight 2026-11-09, then 09:00, 12:00 and 15:00 the same day, and read pr and q05/q25/q50/q95 at tomorrow's noon step as a share of cs.
expected: The 14 whole days behind each tick are the same alternating clear/overcast history, so every tick should fit pr about 1.0 (the clearest days) and the same fan: q05 0.45, q50 0.725, q95 1.0 of clear sky. The plan (5.1) fits the ratio on clear-sky periods and the bands from day residuals, and the live tick runs this every 15 minutes.
evidence: forecast.py:75-87: h0 = t0 - 14*86400 on a 15-minute-aligned t0 and `sl = slice(d*1440, (d+1)*1440)`, so each 'day' runs from the tick's time of day to the same time next day and mixes the afternoon of one local day with the morning of the next. The per-slice ratios k_days average towards the mean, pr = quantile(k, 0.9) (line 92) drops, kn = k/pr (line 93) collapses to about 1 and so do the empirical quantiles kq (line 94). plans.build_problem reads q50 as PV and q25 as PVlo (plans.py:175-176) and optimise.py:306-317 sizes the outage reserve from Lc - PVlo, so an intraday plan can carry a PV q25 57 % above the midnight issue's and a collapsed uncertainty band; the Forecasts page's 'performance ratio' also swings through the day. Fix: slice on local-day boundaries (twin.day_start_utc / (ts+5h)//86400) and drop the partial first/last day.

title: Schedule adherence is updated per 24 h block from the tick time (windows split and pooled), so the posterior depends on when the tick ran and converges per day, not per slot
label: bug
steps: 28 days of 1-minute grid_present with a daily 14:00-16:00 window actually kept on 7 of the 28 days (hit rate 0.25). Call forecast._adherence(windows, grid, _window_mask(windows, ts)) once with the 28-day history starting at local midnight and once with it starting at 15:00 (what outage() builds at a 15:00 tick, h0 = t0 - 28 d).
expected: The same posterior either way: Beta(8,2) prior plus 7 hits in 28 windows = 0.395; per the plan (5.3, R5 4.3, tracker FOR-08 'adherence updates per observed slot') the update is per scheduled slot or window with separate start/end rates, converging in about 20 slots.
actual: 0.395 for the midnight-aligned history, 0.553 for the 15:00-aligned one (0.12 s snippet). A tick inside or after the window inflates adherence by pooling half of today's window with half of tomorrow's; the demo's Faisalabad site has exactly a 14:00-16:00 window.
evidence: forecast.py:310 `day_idx = (np.arange(len(grid)) // 1440)` partitions from h0, line 314 tests `mean(down[sel]) >= 0.5` over all in-window minutes of that block, so two half-windows from different calendar days are one trial and a hit on either counts. The value feeds p_down_s (line 368), the hard g = 0 rule once it passes 0.9 (line 383), the plan header (plans.py:413) and the Outages page KPI (routes_telemetry.py:235). Fix: iterate over window occurrences (local day x window) and count each as one Bernoulli trial.

title: Stage-1 PV with 3-6 days of data: the clearness quantiles are the stage-0 prior because the scaling term divides the median by itself
label: bug
steps: Evaluate line 94 with kn = [0.5, 0.6, 0.55, 0.7] and month_k = 0.88 (any site with 3 to 6 fitted days).
expected: The observed clearness level of the fitted days informs the quantiles (or the code states that the prior is used on purpose below 7 days).
actual: `np.median(kn) / max(1e-6, np.median(kn))` is 1.0, so kq == np.clip(K_PRIOR * month_k / 0.86, 0, 1.1) exactly (checked: [0.307 0.46 0.716 0.88 0.972 1.023 1.044]); the site's data only enters through pr.
evidence: forecast.py:94. The expression is a no-op by construction; the intent was presumably to scale the prior by median(kn) over the prior's own median (month_k). Impact is small because pr absorbs the level, but it is dead code masquerading as a fit and the first week of every new site runs on it.

title: PV fit and PV scoring read curtailed inverter output (pv_power_w) and ignore curtail_w, so zero-export sites fit a low performance ratio and are scored against their own curtailment
label: bug
steps: Demo Faisalabad (regime none, no export cap) or any real zero-export C&I site: once the battery is full late morning, surplus PV is curtailed. twin.simulate writes pv_power_w = available - curtail (twin.py:446, 465) and curtail_w separately (twin.py:468); a real inverter likewise reports produced, i.e. curtailed, PV. After 14 such days call forecast.pv at midnight and, next day, score_day.
expected: The capacity fit (plan 5.1: measured on physical power on clear-sky periods) and the daytime nRMSE use available PV = pv + curtail, which telemetry.minute_grid already exposes as g['curtail'] (telemetry.py:396). The clear-sky ceiling and the forecast describe what the plant can deliver; curtailment is the optimiser's own decision (K[t]).
actual: pvm = g['pv'] (line 81) and k_days (line 87) are computed on curtailed output; the clearest days are also the most curtailed, so pr = quantile(k, 0.9) is biased low and every quantile is capped at pr x cs (line 103-104). score_day uses col = g['pv'] (line 503), so curtailed midday hours count as forecast error and feed the forecast_bust alert and the accuracy tiles. The Forecasts page then shows a 'performance ratio' below 1 on a healthy plant.
evidence: forecast.py:80-87, 103-104, 503; twin.py:446, 465-468; telemetry.py:393-396 (curtail column available). Magnitude not measured here; it scales with the share of days the battery fills before noon.

title: Critical load comes only from the onboarding form, defaults to 0 kW for every hour, and a zero makes the outage reserve rule inert with no warning
label: feature-gap
steps: Onboard a site in the web app leaving 'Critical load' at its default (site-form.ts:74 `critical_load_kw: Array(24).fill(0)`, accepted by the zod rule `v >= 0` at site-form.ts:152), activate it, let a tick run, read the plan steps' critical_kw and the reserve.
expected: Plan Part 4.1 (line 301) and 5.2: Lc[t] is the 75th percentile of observed load during adequately backed outages per hour of day (or from a backup-load point), with the template as fallback and a data-quality warning; the plan's headline value is holding reserve for the next forecast outage.
actual: forecast.load reads twin.critical_share(site) = data.critical_load_kw only (lines 207, 211, 245) and caps it at q75; no learned profile exists (the plan's critical_load_profiles table with source 'learned' is absent). With the default zeros Lc = 0, deficit = max(0, Lc - PVlo) = 0 in optimise.py:310-312, so R[t] is only the sigma widening and no reserve is ever held; activation (routes_sites) and the onboarding review (tab-review.tsx:72 prints '0 kW at most') do not flag it.
evidence: forecast.py:206-211, 245; twin.py:83-85; sites.py:60 default [0.0]*24; optimise.py:306-317; frontend site-form.ts:74,152. The tracker defers the learned estimate to FOR-07 (stage 2), but Part 5.2 places it with censoring, stage-independent, and a silent zero default is a product defect on its own.

title: Load accuracy is scored against shed (censored) minutes and the persistence baseline over a different slot set, so the page shows inflated load nRMSE and a non-comparable baseline
label: bug
steps: A site with a daily 2-hour grid loss during which only the backed-up circuits run (load falls 60 %). forecast.load censors those minutes (lines 201, 152-193) and, correctly, forecasts the full demand. Next day forecast.score_day(site, day) is run by alerts.nightly.
expected: Plan 5.2: censored samples leave the training set and the baselines; the nRMSE should skip censored slots (or score served load against a served-load forecast), and the baseline RMSE should be computed over the same slots as the forecast's so the 'baseline' column on the Forecasts page is like for like.
actual: act = nanmean(g['load']) over all 96 slots (lines 503-504) includes the shed slots, so every outage day charges the forecast with the shed demand; the baseline (lines 517-521) is averaged over okp = ok & ~isnan(pers) while the forecast uses ok, so with gaps last week the two RMSEs cover different slots. The summary tiles (lines 553-556) and ScoresTable then mislead the pilot's 'beats persistence' gate.
evidence: forecast.py:496-522 versus censored_minutes (152-193) and the plan's censoring rule; the same censored_minutes mask is available in score_day via minute_grid.

title: No PV skill or smart-persistence baseline and only one horizon class are scored, although tracker FOR-04 and FOR-10 are marked done
label: spec-mismatch
steps: Open the Forecasts page after a week of scores, or query GET /api/sites/{id}/forecasts/scores: the pv rows carry value only (baseline null) and every row has horizon_class 'day_ahead'.
expected: Plan 5.5 / R5 6: PV skill = 1 - RMSE_model/RMSE_smart_persistence per horizon class (0-2 h, 2-6 h, 6-24 h, 24-48 h), where smart persistence is the clear-sky profile times yesterday's same-hour index (6-24 h) or the last hour's index (0-2 h); the WP5 gate is skill >= 25 % at 6-24 h. FOR-04 ('skill scoring per horizon class') and FOR-10 ('metrics of Part 5.5 by horizon class') are [x] in EMS_BUILD_PROGRESS.md lines 125 and 131.
actual: score_day writes a single 'day_ahead' row per kind (lines 515, 531); the PV row has no baseline_value, so the accuracy tiles show an nRMSE with nothing to judge it against and the product cannot report the gate it pre-registered. The smart-persistence skill exists only inside tests/test_public_data.py.
evidence: forecast.py:484-541; store.py:185-186 (one baseline_value column); frontend accuracy-cards.tsx:52-63 renders what it gets. DESIGN_LOG notes only the Brier climatology column.

title: Unscheduled-outage hazard splits one outage into several at any data gap and the observed-outage walk-back stops at a gap
label: bug
steps: 28 days of 1-minute grid_present with one 2-hour outage a day whose logger drops 3 minutes of rows mid-outage (a logger that browns out when the grid falls, or a CSV source with holes). Call forecast.outage(site, t0); then, with the grid currently down across such a gap, call it with now set and read observed.elapsed_min.
expected: One start a day, median duration about 120 min, lam_day about 1; elapsed counted from the real start. The censoring path already treats gaps this way: _outage_runs (lines 139-149) bridges unknown minutes up to OUTAGE_GAP_MINUTES and 2-sample flickers.
actual: down = _hold(grid, iv - 1) == 0 (line 337) holds nothing for a 1-minute source, NaN reads as up, so starts (line 338) count two events per outage, durations halve (line 343-347) and lam_h doubles (line 359), raising p_start and the reserve priced at p_start * c_short; the walk-back `while obs_grid[k-1] == 0` (lines 394-395) stops at NaN, so elapsed is short and expected_remaining_min long.
evidence: forecast.py:337-347, 359, 392-407 versus _outage_runs 139-149. Not run; from code.

title: Load's last-two-hours ratio compares today's minutes with a reference that includes today's own slot values
label: bug
steps: A site in early stage 1 (2-3 same-day-type days); load the last two hours 30 % above its usual level; call forecast.load(site, t0) and read q50[0].
expected: ratio = recent / median of the same slot on previous days, lifting the first steps by about 30 % (as test_fix_r3 expects with 21 days).
actual: lo15 spans up to t0 (line 213), so for each of the last 120 minutes `lo15[m][-7:]` (line 237) contains today's own value of that slot; with 2 values the median is the mean of yesterday and today, halving the lift toward 1; with 3-7 values it shifts the median whenever today's value sits between the middle ones.
evidence: forecast.py:213-216 build lo15 to t0; 230-241 compute ref from it without excluding the slots inside [t0-7200, t0).

title: The forecast_bust alert threshold (daily nRMSE by nameplate > 0.6) can only be reached by a dead plant, and the plan's 30-minute bust re-solve does not exist
label: bug
steps: Any day with a badly wrong PV forecast (for example a clear-sky forecast on a fog day): run alerts.nightly; grep plans.py/routes_edge.py/scheduler.py for 'bust'.
expected: Plan 2.4 (line 167) and OPT-15: a forecast bust is a PV error above 30 % of the clear-sky ceiling over 30 minutes and triggers an event re-solve; a daily alert should use a threshold forecasts actually cross.
actual: The alert fires only when the day's RMSE exceeds 60 % of the AC nameplate (the RMS of a clear-sky curve itself is about 0.6 of nameplate), i.e. a forecast of full sun against zero output all day; no code re-solves on a bust (no 'bust' in plans, routes_edge or scheduler). The alert text 'missed by X percent (nRMSE)' will in practice never appear.
evidence: alerts.py:372-375; forecast.py:513-515 (nRMSE by kw_ac); EMS_BUILD_PLAN.md line 167; OPT-15 [~] in the tracker lists the bust re-solve.

title: Load day types are Sunday-or-not only: no Pakistan public holidays, Eid, Ramadan or site off days, although FOR-06 is marked done with the holiday calendar
label: spec-mismatch
steps: Forecast an industrial site across Eid (3-4 days at near-zero load) or a public holiday; then forecast the following week.
expected: Plan 5.2 and R5 4.2: equivalent-day persistence by day type (working, half-day, off day, public holiday from the holidays library's Pakistan calendar, Ramadan working day, Eid) with the site's configured off days. Tracker FOR-06 is [x] 'stage 1 equivalent-day persistence with day types and the Pakistan holiday calendar' (EMS_BUILD_PROGRESS.md line 127).
actual: _day_type returns 1 only for Sunday (lines 124-126); the holidays package is not in requirements.txt and SiteFields has no off-day or operating-hours field. A holiday is forecast as a working day (the plan charges the battery for a peak that does not come), and the holiday then sits in the next week's medians for that weekday.
evidence: forecast.py:124-126, 216-222, 236; requirements.txt (no holidays); sites.py SiteFields (no off_days); twin.py:119 notes the twin does not model holidays either, so the demo cannot show the gap.

title: Cold start without an entered schedule treats a rural feeder as almost always up: the DISCO prior covers unscheduled trips only (about 2 h/day on QESCO) instead of the plan's 10 h/day
label: spec-mismatch
steps: Create a QESCO/PESCO/SEPCO site without a load-shedding schedule (the CCMS scraper of FOR-08 is not built, so only manual entry exists) and read the outage forecast's p_down and lam_day.
expected: Plan 5.3 cold start: 'the DISCO's hourly climatology from the fleet, or a hand-entered prior (for example 10 hours a day on QESCO, PESCO and SEPCO feeders; 2 hours on urban LESCO and IESCO) flagged prior on screen'.
actual: prior_day = DISCO_TRIPS[disco] trips per day (QESCO 1.6) times a 75-minute median gives about 2 h/day of expected outage spread over the day; the scheduled hours a rural feeder loses are absent until an operator types the windows, and nothing on screen says the forecast is a prior for that reason (the page says 'No announced schedule yet' only in the adherence cell).
evidence: forecast.py:33-34, 350-359, 362; the twin itself assumes a 14:00-16:00 window for rural DISCOs (twin.py:91-95), so the demo hides it. Frontend forecast-panel.tsx:89.

title: Stage wording says stage 0 lasts 'until the site has a week of its own data' but PV and load reach stage 1 after 3 days
label: ux
steps: Open the Forecasts page on a site with 3-6 days of telemetry.
expected: The stage card's words match the gates: PV and load from about 3 days (forecast.py:88 days_ok >= 3; forecast.py:208 have_days < 3), outage from 7 days of grid readings (forecast.py:408).
actual: STAGE_WORDS for pv and load say 'until the site has a week of its own data' while the badge already reads 'Stage 1'; the Overview notice says Preliminary 'day N of 14'. Three different horizons for the same idea.
evidence: forecast-words.ts:196-200; stage-card.tsx:160; overview-page.tsx:177; backend forecast.py:88, 208, 408.

title: The accuracy tiles' 'last 7 days' is the mean of the last 7 scored rows (any span), and the outage chart draws p_start one slot early
label: ux
steps: A site whose nightly scoring skipped days (completeness < 0.5, a missed nightly job, or no midnight issue): read summary.last7; and compare the 'Outage starts (chance)' bars with p_down on the Forecasts page.
expected: 'nRMSE, last 7 days' covers the last seven calendar days (or says how many days it holds); p_start[t] is by definition the chance an outage starts in step t+1 (plan 4.1 line 303, forecast.py:372-381), so the bar belongs at t[i+1].
actual: vals7 = v[-7:] over whatever rows exist, labelled 'last 7 days' with 'N days scored' only as a subtitle; the chart passes p_start aligned to t (outage-probability-chart.tsx:42) so the start bar appears one 15-minute slot before the step whose p_down it precedes.
evidence: forecast.py:544-557; accuracy-cards.tsx:56-61; forecast-panel.tsx:80-83; outage-probability-chart.tsx:29-50.

title: FOR-02 weather feed not built: every PV forecast is clear sky x climatology x yesterday's ratio, with no NWP, fallback flags or widening
label: feature-gap
steps: Read any pv issue: there is no nwp_source/nwp_run_time/flags; the 24-48 h PV median is cs x pr x the 14-day clearness quantiles regardless of tomorrow's weather.
expected: Plan 5.1 stage 0/1 and 5.6: Open-Meteo hourly NWP downscaled through the clear-sky index, air-quality AOD/dust, a fallback chain with flags and 25 % widening, a health probe; rows carry nwp_run_time, nwp_source and flags.
actual: No provider interface, no weather client, no flags (module docstring lines 1-6 and DESIGN_LOG 'v1 build: Forecasters'). On the public data the day-ahead median only beats same-hour persistence by 0.12-0.21 skill at three sites and loses at Rahim Yar Khan (test_public_data docstring); a weather front (monsoon, fog onset) is invisible until the smart-persistence blend sees it in the first two hours. This is by design pending the owner's Open-Meteo licence (O5), but the product offers no provider status or 'no weather feed' notice (UI-08's weather strip and fallback share are also absent, BACKEND_ASKS.md:28).
evidence: forecast.py:1-6, 65-119; HANDOFF 8.C; tracker FOR-02 [ ]; R5 2.1 and 8; frontend docs/BACKEND_ASKS.md:28.

title: FOR-05/FOR-07 stage-2 models and conformal bands not built: PV bands are 14 daily ratios applied uniformly, load bands a 7-day std with a 6 % floor
label: feature-gap
steps: Inspect a stage-1 pv issue: q05..q95 at every step are cs x pr x a fixed vector of day-level quantiles (no horizon or sky-class dependence); a load issue: med +- z x max(std of up to 7 values, 0.06 med).
expected: Plan 5.1/5.2: conformal residual bands by horizon class and sky class from day 3, the xgboost residual model from week 4-6 (FOR-05), the direct multi-horizon load model with belief-time-safe lags (FOR-07), coverage of q10-q90 at 80 +- 5 % and q05-q95 at 90 % by stage 2, reported with pinball/CRPS.
actual: Only stages 0 and 1 exist; no pinball, CRPS or coverage is computed, so the bands' calibration is never measured (the optimiser's PVlo = q25 and Lhi = q75 depend on it). Deferred by design (DESIGN_LOG, tracker [ ]); the gap worth noting is that FOR-04's 'conformal bands' acceptance is claimed [x] while the bands are empirical day quantiles with no horizon dependence.
evidence: forecast.py:91-99, 225-227; tracker FOR-04 [x], FOR-05 [ ], FOR-07 [ ]; plan 5.5 probabilistic row.

title: Bill rebuild prices the whole reading interval with the versions in force on the reading date; the optimiser and ledger price each day with that day's version
label: bug
steps: 1. Take a B-2(b) connection with reading_day=20 and a flat 100 kW import (MDI block placed elsewhere). 2. Call tariffs.rebuild for 2026-01-21..2026-02-20: every line uses SRO 279 (off-peak 22.83, schedule resolved at period_end, line 520). Bumping one kWh at 25 Jan 03:00 changes bearable_rs by 26.45. 3. Call tariffs.vectors for 25 Jan 2026 00:00 PKT: c_imp off-peak is 31.10 = (27.41 January card + 3.23 DSS) x 1.015 (card resolved at t0, line 688). The ledger (verify._minute_prices) also prices 25 Jan at 31.10. The same applies to calendar_for, _tax_factor_energy, icp_rule and prosumer (all resolved at `on = period_end`, lines 517-522, 555, 608, 611). A calendar-month February 2026 bill likewise bills 1-11 Feb at SRO 279.
expected: Plan Part 4 makes it a governing rule that every optimiser coefficient equals the bill engine's marginal price. Plan 6.1 leaves the February proration open and gates the 2% rebuild on re-running at the first 2027 bill. A reading interval that spans a schedule's effective date should be priced per day by the version in force (DISCOs bill such intervals pro rata by days), or by one documented rule shared by the bill engine, the vectors and the ledger.
actual: rebuild() resolves the schedule, calendar, taxes, ICP and prosumer version once, at period_end, and prices consumption from before the new version's start at the new rates. The vectors and ledger use the day's own version. On the same kWh they disagree by Rs 4.65 (31.10 vs 26.45), and the rebuilt bill differs from a pro-rata DISCO bill. This will hit every mid-month reading interval across the 1 Jan 2027 rebasing, 53 days away.
evidence: tariffs.py:517-523 (`on = period_end`; card_for, calendar_for, _tax_factor_energy all at `on`), 555 icp_rule(on), 608/611 prosumer(on); vectors at 687-690 use `on = t0` local date. Probe in the scratchpad: bill marginal 26.45 against vector 31.10 for 25 Jan 2026 03:00.

title: Rebuilt bill floors at zero and discards the excess export credit (no carry-forward); bearable_rs goes negative
label: bug
steps: 1. Take an A-2(c) connection on net_metering_legacy. 2. Rebuild October 2026 with 20 kW import all day and 300 kW export from 09:00 to 15:00, so the off-peak period ends in surplus. 3. Result: total_rs 0.0, credits_rs 1,525,510, gross bill before credit about 326,753, recovered_taxes_rs 79,157.51, bearable_rs -79,157.51. 4. Nothing records the unused credit, so the next month's rebuild starts with no brought-forward balance. The same applies to net_billing when exports x NAEPP exceed the gross bill.
expected: Plan 6.3 step 9 and R9 13 step 9 say the bill never goes negative, but the excess credit rolls to the next cycle, or is paid quarterly under Prosumer reg. 14(2). Legacy sites need carry-forward balances (R9 17.7; tracker TAR-02, marked [x], lists "settlement and carry-forward"). The bearable cost of a zero bill cannot be below zero unless a carried credit is accounted for.
actual: `total = max(0.0, bill_amount + s235 + flat - credit)` silently drops the credit beyond the bill. bearable_rs = total - recovered then subtracts GST and s.235 that the floor already absorbed, giving a negative bearable cost. There is no carry-forward state anywhere. The vectors still value every surplus kWh at the surplus or NAEPP rate, so in surplus months the optimiser and ledger disagree with the rebuilt bill. Both the surplus month and the following month differ from the DISCO's bill.
evidence: tariffs.py:604-611 (credit), 637-639 (floor, recovered, bearable). grep finds no carry/brought-forward state in backend/gridlytics. Probe output: `3 legacy total 0.0 bearable -79157.51 recovered 79157.51 credit 1525510.0`.

title: FCA recognised only by the exact key "fca": a second FCA on the same bill drops out of the ICP price, and its negative-FCA exemption is lost
label: bug
steps: 1. Take an ICP-eligible B-2(b) connection whose November 2026 off-peak total is above its baseline. 2. With the shipped adders, the vectors' above-case c_imp is 23.325 and the rebuild's 1-kWh marginal is 23.32 (they agree). 3. Approve an adder with key "fca_sep", +2.5624, billing_months ["2026-11"]. adders_for's docstring says two months' FCAs billed together are two keys, and R9 6.2 says NEPRA bundles FCAs or moves one to the next bill. Now the vector stays at 23.325 while the bill charges 25.93 per ICP kWh. 4. Approve "fca_aug_neg" at -1.5 with negative_exempt_icp True. The bill now charges it on the ICP units (24.41) although the rule exempts them; the vector is still 23.325. 5. verify.summary's fca_billed (verify.py:1097) treats a month whose FCA has another key as not yet billed.
expected: Positive FCAs apply to ICP incremental units and negative FCAs do not (R9 5, SRO 2409), whatever key a bundled or late FCA is stored under. The optimiser's ICP price must equal the bill's (plan Part 4 rule, OPT-06).
actual: vectors' add_icp sums only `a["key"] == "fca" and rate > 0` (line 697). rebuild exempts a negative FCA from ICP units only when `a["key"] == "fca"` (line 596). verify checks `a["key"] == "fca"`. A second FCA key therefore makes the optimiser under-price ICP units by that FCA x 1.015, and a negative second FCA is wrongly charged on ICP units.
evidence: tariffs.py:596, 697; verify.py:1097. Probe output: `A no 2nd FCA: vec 23.325 above bill 23.32`, `B +fca_sep 2.5624: vec 23.325 bill 25.93`, `C +neg fca under own key: vec 23.325 bill 24.41`.

title: Legacy net-metering surplus credited at the consumer's off-peak tariff (A-2(c) 35.15) instead of the NAPPP the only primary source gives (Rs 25.32)
label: spec-mismatch
steps: 1. Look at the shipped net_metering_legacy body: surplus_rate "off_peak", accounting_rate 25.32 (never read). 2. For an A-2(c) legacy site (the demo's Lahore mall) with a period ending in surplus, tariffs._legacy_surplus_rate returns 35.15, and vectors set c_imp = s_rate and c_exp = s_rate - 0.01 (test_legacy_surplus_period_moves_only_the_bare_credit asserts 35.15). 3. For B-2(b) the credit is 22.83.
expected: R9 8.2 [P], SRO 1501(I)/2026 para 23: net-metering exports are accounted for at the notified NAPPP of Rs 25.32/kWh for Q2 CY2026. The press figure of Rs 26-27 for the old buyback also matches NAPPP, not a tariff's off-peak rate. The "off-peak rate" rule rests only on R9 8.3 [S] (the 2015 regulations were not read). The surplus credit should default to the notified NAPPP and be versioned per quarter, with off-peak as the override a legacy bill can confirm.
actual: The default credits A-2(c) surplus at 35.15 (39% above 25.32) and B-2(b) at 22.83 (10% below). This feeds the rebuilt bill, the ledger and the optimiser's value of exporting versus storing PV at legacy sites. The 25.32 is stored but unused and not versioned per quarter.
evidence: tariff_data.py:122-124; tariffs.py:498-503 (_legacy_surplus_rate), 726-749 (vectors), 610-611 (rebuild credit); R9 sections 0.6, 8.2 and 8.3; plan 6.1 'Legacy net metering' row.

title: Tax flags, ICP eligibility and baseline, and Tariff F season cannot be set from the web app; every web-made connection is priced as a sales-tax-registered taxpayer, and strn=false still recovers GST
label: feature-gap
steps: 1. Onboard any site in the web app. connectionBody sends `tax: {...saved, province}` and passes the saved icp, seasonal_multiplier and season_months through unchanged. No field exists for strn, gst_recoverable, s235_adjustable, atl, ICP eligibility or baseline, or season months (grep finds no gst_recoverable, strn or ICP eligible field anywhere in frontend/src outside display cards). 2. The backend defaults (sites.TaxFlags) are gst_recoverable=True, s235_adjustable=True, strn=True. 3. A no-STRN A-2 or A-3 site therefore gets energy_factor 1.015 instead of about 1.376 = 1.015 x (1 + 0.03 + 0.18 + 0.12 x 1.21). 4. Through the API, saving tax {strn:false} alone charges the 3% further tax but keeps gst_recoverable=True, so GST is still excluded from the bearable price. 5. evidence: site-form.ts:197-209 (connectionBody); sites.py:95-107 (IcpBaseline, TaxFlags defaults); tariffs.py:463-478 (_tax_factor_energy reads strn and gst_recoverable separately); tracker TAR-10 [ ].

title: After 1 Jan 2027 the engine silently keeps pricing with the CY2026 schedule: nothing flags the passed 'awaiting notification' placeholder

title: No hand-worked golden bill exists: every bill-engine test compares the engine with itself, yet TAR-06 is marked done

A site saved without lat defaults to 31 and gets it too. 2. title: ICP at legacy net-metering sites compares net imports with the baseline, instead of capping gross-import increments at net imports pro rata

Off-peak period: imports 2,000, exports 2,500, baseline 1,000. rebuild nets first (lines 549-553), then ICP-splits the net (557-561): peak incremental 500, off-peak 0, with 500 kWh of surplus. R9 5 and R9 13 step 4: incremental = max(0, imports - baseline) per period (500 + 1,000), capped at total net import (3,000 - 2,500 = 500), then split pro rata (about 167 peak, 333 off-peak). The bills differ by about 333 kWh x (35.68 - 22.83).
