title: Plan sheds load with the grid up to avoid MDI rises (U <= L on grid-up steps), labelled self_consumption/idle and not caught by the guard
label: bug
steps:
1. In solve(): base_served = L where g=1, U_ub = base_served (L262-264), and U costs H*voll (L269). So U <= L on every grid-up step.
2. MDI rows (L463-470): sum(G over a 30-min block) <= 2*M, with a duplicate row that adds (Lhi - L). M costs rate_mdi per kW: Rs 1,250/kW-month before the tax gross-up for B-2/B-3/A-2(c) in tariff_data.py L38-46.
3. Shedding 1 kW for one 30-min block costs VoLL*0.5 h = Rs 250 at the default VoLL of 500. So for up to about 5 blocks, shedding is cheaper than raising M by 1 kW.
4. Repro from code: test_fix_optimiser._problem(T=96), plus p['mdi'] = {rate:1250, M0:100, floor:0, n_mdi:2, G_elapsed:0, n_elapsed:0, month_end_step:96}, L[40:44] = 300 and battery E0 = 25. solve() returns U > 0 at steps 40-43 with g = 1. explain() names those steps 'idle' or 'self_consumption'.
5. VoLL accepts 0 (sites.py L61, ge=0.0). With VoLL below c_imp, the plan sheds every grid-up step instead of importing, and Hold floors and reserve slack become free.
6. Real data, scratch DB, mall plan with belief time 2026-10-30T07:00Z: on 1 Nov, 11:15 G=75 U=184.5 and 11:30 G=10 U=267.6 (L=391 kW, grid present). Breakdown unserved_rs = 77,070. status_label is 'Solved within tolerance', and the reasons are self_consumption and idle.
7. Real data, feed mill plan with belief time 2026-11-04T01:00Z: 07:45 G=771 U=68.5, reason 'idle'.
expected: A grid-connected C&I site cannot shed load on command: Mode A and Mode B have no load-shed primitive, and the twin imports instead. U should be allowed only where the grid is down, or only for load above G_max. VoLL should have a sane lower bound, at least the highest import price. Part 7.1 step 8 says the wrong-plan guard must refuse a plan whose own grid draw exceeds mdi_cap_kw, and plans._guard's docstring claims this check. That check would catch such plans in the replay.
actual: The optimiser buys MDI headroom by shedding real (q50) load, partly to make room under M for hypothetical q75 load. The plan page shows hundreds of kW unserved with the grid up, the battery dispatch is built around this fiction, and on site the meter's MDI rises above the plan's cap. explain() never says 'unserved' for grid-up steps. plans._guard (L327-347) checks only the SoC floor and import during an outage, so these plans go out as active.
evidence: optimise.py L262-269 (U bounds and cost), L463-470 (mdi and mdi_hi rows), L787-826 (explain's grid-up branch has no unserved rule); sites.py L61 voll ge=0.0; plans.py L327-347 (_guard has no MDI check despite its docstring); plan Part 4.3 'Unserved critical load: 0 <= U[t] <= Lserved[t]' with Lserved = L when the grid is up. Read-only scratch-DB query: 8 of 484 plans shed with the grid up (mall 5, feed mill 3). Example figures as in steps 6-7.

title: Billing-month start: M2 (and M on day 1) anchored at the MDI floor, so the plan drains the battery off-peak to hold the whole month's MDI at 25% of sanctioned load
label: spec-mismatch
steps:
1. When the horizon crosses the billing-month end, M2 = m.var(..., lb=mdi['floor'], cost=rate) (L459-461). floor = floor_share x sanctioned load (tariffs.vectors L755: 0.25 x 650 = 162.5 kW for the mall).
2. On the first ticks of a month, M0 is about 0 (plans.month_to_date has few full blocks), so M's lower bound = max(M0, floor) is also about the floor (L454).
3. Every kW above the floor in the first 1-2 days of the month is therefore priced as a certain full-month MDI rise, although the rest of the month will almost surely set a higher peak.
4. Real data, scratch DB, mall plan with belief time 2026-10-30T07:00Z, 1 Nov: 09:30-11:15 the battery discharges at 50 kW off-peak (c_imp 39.48) from SoC 95% to 10%. Each block is held at (G1 + G2 + (Lhi - L))/2 of about 162.5 kW, exactly the floor (e.g. 10:00 + 10:15: 170 + 128). Nothing is left for the evening peak, and load is shed (see the grid-up shed finding).
5. Also: plans.tick passes only res['M'][0] as the slot grid_cap (L448), so slots in the next month carry the old month's cap.
expected: A kW is worth its expected effect on the billed MDI. Early in a month (and for M2), anchor M/M2 to an expected month peak: last month's MDI, or the forecast max of (Lhi - P_dis). R3 6.3's previous-peak lower bound assumes a meaningful month-to-date peak.
actual: The plan spends the battery (and sheds load) on the new month's first morning to defend a month MDI at the floor that the site will exceed anyway. This loses the peak-window arbitrage on day 1 of every month.
evidence: optimise.py L454 (M lb max(M0, floor)), L459-461 (M2 lb floor), L465; plans.py L206-209, L448; tariffs.py L753-756. Scratch-DB plan steps as listed. Plan Part 4.3 specifies 'M2 with floor M_floor', so the design itself is the cause.

title: A battery that starts below soc_min makes the tick infeasible when it cannot recharge: the terminal row forces E[T] >= soc_min
label: bug
steps:
1. E_use has lb 0 (L406). The terminal row is E_use - E[T] <= -Emin (L407), so E[T] >= Emin + E_use >= Emin is a hard constraint.
2. E's lower bound is min(Emin, E0) (L279-281), so a start below the band is accepted at t = 0.
3. Take a site with grid_charge_allowed = False whose PV never exceeds load in 48 h (winter fog, a mill whose load exceeds PV), or a charge_block override running to the horizon end. charge_surplus (L296-303) or the bound forces C = 0.
4. Repro: test_fix_optimiser._problem() with battery E0 = 10 (5%), soc_min 0.1, a_grid False, PV = 0. optimise.solve() reports HiGHS infeasible, so status is not_solved. solve_with_policy's relaxed 24 h retry is equally infeasible, and plans.tick stores 'failed' every tick until the SoC rises.
5. Existing test test_a_battery_starting_below_the_floor_is_planned_not_held passes only because grid charging is allowed.
expected: Part 4.3 and 4.5: 'An E0 outside the band enters through EMHASS's single-recovery rows ... never a 422', 'no routine state is infeasible'. R2 3.5: an unrecoverable battery has the band switched off for the run. The terminal value should value stored energy, not impose a floor (e.g. free sign on E_use, or bound by E[T] - min(Emin, E0)).
actual: A routine state (battery at or below its configured floor after native operation or an outage, grid charging off, no PV surplus) fails every tick. The previous plan stays active and stales, and plan_failed alerts follow.
evidence: optimise.py L279-283, L404-407; DESIGN_LOG 'The terminal value applies to the energy above the floor (E_use <= E[T] - E_min)' states the intent, which was valuation, not a hard floor; plans._guard L342 accepts a start below the band, so the case is expected.

title: An out-of-band start relaxes the SoC floor for the whole horizon: plans may discharge back below soc_min later, and Mode B forwards that floor
label: spec-mismatch
steps:
1. e_lb = full(T+1, min(Emin, E0)) applies at every step, not only until the battery first re-enters the band (L279-281).
2. Take E0 = 5% with soc_min = 10% and grid charging allowed. The plan charges off-peak, discharges into the evening peak down to 5% (an extra 10 kWh on a 200 kWh pack at a peak/off-peak spread of about Rs 20/kWh), then recharges to soc_min by T because of the terminal row.
3. The plan's steps carry soc_pct = 5. delivery._mode_b_floor (L231-237) returns min(reserve_pct, soc_pct), so a Mode B edge is told it may discharge to 5%.
4. plans._guard (L343) tolerates min(soc_min, soc0) - 0.02, so the plan passes.
expected: Use EMHASS single-recovery as Part 4.3 and R2 3.5 specify: while unrecovered the SoC may only move towards the band, and once it is in the band the band binds for the rest of the horizon.
actual: The configured lower limit is lost for the whole 48 h whenever a tick starts below it. Mode A clamps floors at max(bms_low + 2, fallback), so the plan and the device diverge. Mode B passes the below-band floor to the edge.
evidence: optimise.py L279-283; delivery.py L231-237; plans.py L342-344; R2-emhass.md L135 (single recovery: 'while unrecovered the SoC may only move towards the band').

title: Fuel available is never carried: every tick plans on a full tank (state.fuel_l is never written), and tank_l = 0 means unlimited fuel
label: feature-gap
steps:
1. build_problem sets fuel_available = float(site.state.get('fuel_l', tank_l) or 1e9).
2. grep shows no writer of 'fuel_l' to site_state. sites.put_state is called only for active_plan, last_tick, edge_*, tier_signoff, soc and similar. The fuel log (routes_telemetry L374-395) only stores events, and genset_fuel_l telemetry is burn per minute, not a level.
3. So fuel_available always equals the tank's capacity. The demo farm (400 L tank, 47-91 L/day) and every off-grid site plan with 400 L at every tick.
4. The fuel_cap row, the soc_threshold z rows ('tank empty'), the shed-rule re-solve's 'fuel left' test and the threshold repair all read this value, so none of them ever sees a nearly empty tank.
5. A tank_l of 0, which demo.py uses for piped gas, becomes 1e9 through `or 1e9`. GensetFields.tank_l (sites.py L178, ge=0) documents no such meaning, so an HSD set entered with 0 gets unlimited fuel.
expected: Plan Part 4.1 lists 'fuel available' from site state, and Part 4.8 lists it among the state carried between ticks. Track the level from logged fills minus metered or estimated burn (or a tank-level sensor), and make 'unlimited' an explicit flag (e.g. fuel_kind gas_captive).
actual: The plan never rations fuel. At an off-grid or outage-heavy site with a low tank it schedules runs the tank cannot supply, and on site the set stops and load is shed unplanned.
evidence: plans.py L244; grep 'fuel_l' over backend/gridlytics finds only plans.py L244 as a reader and no writer; demo.py L76 (tank_l 0 for gas) and L81 (farm note 'tank-level metering'); optimise.py L241-242, L245-256, L553-560.

title: With gen_charge_allowed = False the genset follow cap is off, so the plan can run the set to carry the load while PV charges the battery (round 4/5 loophole reopened)
label: bug
steps:
1. build_problem sets battery.a_gen_surplus = gen_charge_allowed (plans.py L261). genset_surplus_steps returns all False when a_gen_surplus is False (optimise.py L923-924).
2. Then P_on = S on grid-down steps (L173), with no genset_follow_cap.
3. The charge source row at an outage or off-grid step is C + K <= PV (L288-295). The balance is PV - K + D + P = served - U + C.
4. The plan can set P = served (the set carries the whole load) and C = PV: PV charges the battery while the set carries load PV could have carried. That is genset charging in net terms.
5. twin.simulate's outage branch runs gen = min(S, max(f_min S, served - PV)) whatever the flag (twin.py L407-410), so on site PV serves the load first and the battery gets only PV beyond the load.
6. At an off-grid site this pays: daytime set marginal about a*c_fuel + c_om, roughly Rs 84/kWh, against night low-load operation at about Rs 143/kWh for the farm's 48 kW set.
expected: Round 5 says the follow cap 'closes the PV charges while the set carries the load loophole'. The cap max(f_min S, served - PV) reflects inverter physics and should apply on every grid-down step whatever the charging flag. Only the minimum-load surplus's access to the battery should depend on gen_charge_allowed.
actual: Sites that disallow genset charging get plans counting on battery charge the site never delivers. This is the round-4 failure mode at the farm: the battery near its floor after runs, then rescue starts.
evidence: optimise.py L109, L173, L288-295, L916-925; plans.py L258-261; twin.py L404-417; DESIGN_LOG Round 5 first bullet. No test covers a_gen_surplus = False (grep tests).

title: The plan starts from a stale SoC and does not widen its uncertainty: battery.state uses the last reading up to 30 days old and freezes sigma at that reading
label: bug
steps:
1. battery.state(site, t0) reads minute_grid over the last 30 days, takes last = the index of the last known SoC, and returns soc = est[last] (L29-30).
2. sigma = 1 + 0.19*hours + 2*throughput/E_nom, with hours = (last - a)/60 (L33-36). That is anchor to last reading, not anchor to now.
3. plans.build_problem takes E0 = soc_pct*E_nom and sigma0 from that result (L251-256) with no age check.
4. Repro: stop telemetry for 6 h on a site. The next tick plans from the 6 h old SoC with the same sigma as when data stopped, so the reserve's 2-sigma widening does not grow and the plan is published active.
expected: Part 4.6 and R6: sigma grows with hours since the last anchor, which includes the time with no data. Tracker item OPT-08 calls for 'acquire with per-source staleness'. A stale SoC should widen sigma by the time since the last reading (or cap the plan's confidence) and set a data-quality flag on the plan.
actual: A plan can run from a battery state hours or days old, with a small reserve margin. The only signal is the separate data_stale alert. Mode B setpoints and Mode A targets follow the wrong SoC path.
evidence: battery.py L21-39; plans.py L251-256; alerts.py L59-72 (data_stale alert only, nothing in plans).

title: Wall-clock limits (HANDOFF 8.A.3): any time-limited incumbent, whatever its gap, supersedes the last plan, and the relaxed retry publishes genset runs shorter than min up
label: feature-gap
steps:
1. Model.solve uses HiGHS time_limit in wall-clock seconds (optimise.py L65). Under CPU load more solves stop at 10 s with a weaker incumbent.
2. plans.tick publishes status 'active' whenever the guard passes (L454-469). res['mip_gap'] is only stored, so a plan with a 30% gap replaces a previous optimal plan, and the Mode A table and genset requests follow it.
3. When the first solve finds no incumbent in time, solve_with_policy runs the relaxed retry with UT = DT = 1 (optimise.py L123, L848-861). That 24 h plan is published active too, so alerts.genset_requests can ask a manual-start operator for a 15-minute run on a set whose min_up is 1-2 h.
4. scheduler.tick_company solves every site in series in one thread (scheduler.py L20-36). Off-grid threshold sites can take 3 limits (30 s), and with coalesce and max_instances = 1 a pass longer than 15 minutes skips ticks.
expected: Before superseding the previous plan, compare the new incumbent's gap or objective with the previous plan re-priced on the new inputs, and keep the old one (or re-solve when idle) if the new one is worse. Re-impose min up/down on the relaxed retry (e.g. fix runs to UT), or do not publish genset requests from it. Long term, use a deterministic work limit (HANDOFF 8.A.3).
actual: Plan quality, and so money and genset operations, depends on machine load, and nothing stops a degraded plan from being published. time_limited_recent only counts these plans.
evidence: plans.py L449-469, L557-579; optimise.py L65, L123, L500-505, L840-861; alerts.py L217-260; scheduler.py L20-36, L70-73; DESIGN_LOG Round 4 'The limits themselves are unchanged'.

title: The reserve row on the step before a deterministic outage double-charges the shortfall
label: spec-mismatch
steps:
1. forecast.outage sets g = 0 for scheduled windows with adherence > 0.9 (forecast.py L383) and p_start[t] = adherence on the step before each window (L373-381).
2. optimise writes reserve rows wherever g[t] = 1 and p_start >= 0.01 (L313-317), including the step just before a modelled (g = 0) window. That row is priced at about 0.9 x c_short.
3. The balance rows inside the window already price the same energy (genset fuel or VoLL on U).
expected: Part 4.3: 'No reserve row exists for steps with g[t] = 0: the balance row governs inside an outage', and 'a shortfall is never charged twice'. Drop reserve rows where g[t+1] = 0.
actual: Before each high-adherence load-shedding window the plan pays twice for any shortfall: the reserve slack plus the window's genset or VoLL cost. It over-holds the battery and inflates the objective.
evidence: optimise.py L305-317; forecast.py L371-383.

title: Terminal value: c_cal_hold is a one-step calendar slope, not the holding cost until the next peak (unit error)
label: bug
steps:
1. Part 4.4 defines v_end = eta_d*c_next - c_cyc - c_cal_hold, where c_cal_hold is the calendar cost of holding the energy until the next peak.
2. plans.py L276 sets c_cal_hold = mean(b_cal[:32]). b_cal is in Rs per kWh per 15-minute step (calendar_slope: about 0.034 at 25 C and 0.06 at 35 C).
3. Energy at the horizon end is held 0-24 h (up to 96 steps) before the next peak, so the right figure is about 1-6 Rs/kWh (10 at 45 C), against the 0.03-0.1 subtracted.
expected: c_cal_hold = the sum of b_cal over the steps from the horizon end to the next peak window, e.g. mean slope x hours-to-peak x 4.
actual: v_end is overstated by about Rs 1-10/kWh, so plans hold slightly more energy at hour 48 than the plan's own economics justify.
evidence: plans.py L276; optimise.py L405, L973-978.

title: Grid-tied terminal value never uses the genset's marginal cost on outage-heavy feeders
label: spec-mismatch
steps:
1. c_next = max(c_imp[-96:]) for every grid-tied site (L271). lam_day only switches R_next (L274-275).
2. Part 4.4: c_next is 'the highest all-in marginal import price ... or the genset's marginal cost when that day's outage probability exceeds the site threshold'.
3. At an outage-heavy genset site (e.g. FESCO textile mill, genset marginal about Rs 100+ against peak about Rs 45) stored energy at the horizon end is undervalued.
expected: Use _gen_marginal (or c_short) as c_next when the day after the horizon has outage probability above reserve_policy.p_threshold.
actual: The import peak price is always used, so plans run the battery down toward hour 48 more than they should before likely outages.
evidence: plans.py L271-276; plan Part 4.4 terminal-value paragraph.

title: Cost breakdown omits the next-month MDI (M2), and the terminal credit ignores the E_use cap
label: bug
steps:
1. _breakdown computes mdi_rise_rs from out['M'][0] only (L741-743). M2's cost (rate x M2, at least the floor) is in the objective but in no breakdown line.
2. terminal_credit_rs = -v_end*max(0, E[T] - Emin) (L746), but the objective credits only E_use <= P_dis*H_peak + R_next.
3. Real data, scratch mall plan with belief time 2026-10-30T07:00Z: mdi_rise_rs 0.0, although the plan shed and drained the battery to keep M2 at the floor.
expected: The breakdown's lines add up to the objective: include M2's rise and cap the terminal credit at the optimal E_use.
actual: The plan page's cost lines do not explain the objective and hide the MDI term that drives month-boundary behaviour.

title: month_to_date counts missing minutes as zero import, and its 80% block-completeness check counts grid minutes, not known ones
label: bug
area: optimiser inputs / MDI and ICP month-to-date
steps:
1. minute_grid returns a dense 1-minute grid with NaN for missing minutes, and month_to_date applies nan_to_num to imp (L64).
2. full = bincount(inv) >= interval*0.8 (L83) counts every grid minute, so every closed block is 'full' whatever its data.
3. An edge offline 20 minutes inside the month's peak block gives M0 = (known minutes)/30 of the true mean, so M0 is understated. The mtd per-period imports that set the ICP case (tariffs.vectors q_net) are understated likewise.
expected: Count only known minutes towards completeness, and skip or extrapolate incomplete blocks and periods, as the forecasters already do ('count minutes of data').
actual: After telemetry gaps the plan pays for MDI headroom the bill already has, which feeds the grid-up shedding finding, and can pick the wrong ICP case, which prices every step of that period.
evidence: plans.py L59-91; telemetry.py L377-407 (dense grid, NaN for missing minutes).

title: Perfect-foresight bound leaves the unserved and MDI terms out of its cost and accepts time-limited solves
label: bug
steps:
1. verify._bound builds a hindsight problem with build_problem, so it has MDI rows and U <= L with the grid up, and calls optimise.solve(p, time_limit=5.0) (L787-801).
2. cost = energy_rs + genset_rs + wear_rs (L804). unserved_rs and the MDI rise are excluded, although the solve traded against them.
3. A hindsight solve that sheds load (grid-up MDI shedding, or VoLL against the genset in an outage) lowers energy_rs and counts the shed energy as saving. A 'feasible' (time-limited) result is also accepted, which is not an upper bound.
expected: Price the bound on the same terms the solve minimised (or forbid grid-up U), and treat a time-limited hindsight solve as no bound.
actual: perfect_foresight_rs can be inflated or deflated, which distorts the capture-ratio KPI.
evidence: verify.py L771-806; optimise.py L262-269.

title: The sigma_high alert promises a full re-anchoring charge that no code plans
label: ux
steps:
1. battery.state raises sigma_high above 15 points with the text 'the plan will ask for a full charge to re-anchor' (L54-55). alerts.py L142-144 shows it to users.
2. grep 'anchor' finds nothing in optimise.py, plans.py or delivery.py: no anchor-slot request or full-charge target is ever added to the problem.
expected: Part 4.6 and OPT-10: when sigma exceeds 15 points, the optimiser is asked for an anchor slot (a full charge). Until that exists, the alert must not claim it.
actual: Users are told a corrective action will happen, and it does not.
evidence: battery.py L54-55; alerts.py L139-144; no 'anchor' in optimise.py, plans.py or delivery.py.

title: The wrong-plan guard can never refuse a plan: both of its checks can never trigger
label: bug
area: delivery / wrong-plan guard (Part 7.1 step 8, R6 C2)
steps: 1) Read plans._guard (327-347). It refuses when min replayed SoC < min(bat.soc_min, soc0) - 0.02, or when sim['imp'] > 0 on steps where the grid is down. 2) In twin.simulate every discharge path (dis_room, dis_room_abs, the peak-shave 'extra' at 349, and the outage branch at 412/425) is bounded so that e >= e_min = plant.soc_min*e_nom. plant.soc_min and bat['soc_min'] both come from the battery asset, so SoC can never go below min(soc_min, soc0). 3) out['imp'] is only written in the grid-present branch (twin.py 355-358), so 'import_in_outage' is always 0. 4) Probe: an export slot with soc_floor 0, an 80 kW load, half the day grid-down and a 1 kW grid cap gives min soc 0.1, no guard trip, and import in outage 0.0. 5) In the scratch demo, 0 of 121 plans per site were ever 'held'. The only test that touches _guard monkeypatches it (tests/test_fix_r3_optimiser.py:216).
expected: Part 7.1 step 8 and R6 C2: refuse to sign, and keep the previous plan, when the replayed SoC crosses the absolute (fallback) floor, export exceeds the export floor, the plan's own grid draw exceeds mdi_cap_kw, a genset slot falls where the grid is expected present, or the whole-table safety of step 6 fails. Also, at minimum, a check that critical load is served (sim['unserved'] > 0) on forecast outage steps.
actual: _guard always returns None. No compiled table has ever been refused, and the spec's checks (fallback floor, MDI cap, export floor, genset slot, safe tail, unserved critical load) do not exist. summary.guard is always null.
evidence: plans.py:341-347 (the two checks). twin.py:304-307, 349, 412, 425 (every discharge is bounded at e_min). twin.py:355-358 (imp written only when g). Probe output: 'min soc 0.1 guard trips floor? False import in outage 0.0'. Scratch DB: plan statuses for every demo site are [('active',1),('superseded',120)], with no 'held'.

title: The optimiser plans SoC down to the BMS soc_min, but Mode A floors and the fallback hold 20 %: the plan counts on energy the device will not deliver
label: bug
area: plan vs delivery consistency (Part 7.1 step 5, R6 I2)
steps: 1) optimise.py:273/279 sets the SoC lower bound to Emin = bat['soc_min']*En (default 0.10). 2) delivery.compile_mode_a:109/165 clamps every slot floor to lo = max(bms_low+2, reserve_policy.min_soc_pct), which is 20 by default. The fallback block carries min_soc_floor_pct 20, which U3 says the edge enforces whatever the slots say. 3) Scratch demo feed mill (500 kWh, Sungrow): all 40 recent plans plan grid-up SoC below 20 %. The active plan discharges at 250 kW at 19:00 down to 15.7 % and 13.4 %, on peak steps at c_imp 40.02 Rs/kWh, and reaches 10.0 % at 07:00. The compiled discharge slots have soc_floor_pct 20.0. 4) mode_b() (delivery.py:231-243) sends soc_floor_pct = min(reserve_pct, soc_pct) = 10.0 on 176 steps, below both its own fallback floor (20) and the BMS low cap + 2. Textile: 11 of 40 plans; mall: 2 of 40.
expected: The MILP mirrors the floor delivery enforces (Part 7.3: the edge's safety order is mirrored as hard rows): on grid-up steps E >= max(BMS low+2, fallback floor). Mode B floors are clamped the same way Mode A floors are.
actual: The plan's peak discharge and objective count on 10 % of capacity (50 kWh at the feed mill, about Rs 2,000 of peak energy a day) that the compiled table, the twin replay and an edge applying the fallback all hold back. That energy is imported at peak instead. Plan savings are overstated, and the planned schedule is not what runs. This is the same class of defect as DESIGN_LOG 'The demo's negative savings'. Mode B steps contradict the plan's own fallback floor.
evidence: optimise.py:273 'Emin, Emax = bat["soc_min"] * En', with the E lower bound at 279. delivery.py:109 'lo = max(bms_low_pct + 2, fallback_floor_pct)' and 165 clip. plans.py:446 fallback_floor = reserve_policy.min_soc_pct. delivery.py:234-237 has no clamp. Probe: 'mode B floors min 10.0 steps with floor < fallback 20: 176'; '19:00 2026-11-09 soc 15.7 discharge 250.0 c_imp 40.02'; 'Karachi feed mill ... planning grid-up SoC below the 20% delivery floor: 40' (of 40).

title: Edge sequence numbers are a per-site high-water mark: a reset or out-of-order batch is acknowledged as 'duplicate' and silently dropped
label: bug
steps: 1) Telemetry: _seq_check returns seq > last (routes_edge.py:90-92, telemetry.next_seq 622-630). Events: the claim refuses msg.seq <= max(floor, claim) (331). 2) Case A: the edge sends batch seq 10, which times out or gets a 5xx before it is stored. It then sends seq 11, which succeeds, and retries 10. The answer is {'ack':10,'duplicate':True}, the rows are never stored, and an edge that purges by ack loses them for good. 3) Case B: the edge box is replaced at handover or loses its counter on reboot and restarts at seq 0. Every telemetry and events batch is answered 'duplicate' until the counter passes the old high-water mark. Readings, outage_start events (OPT-15 re-solves) and readback_mismatch/local_override events (pauses) are all lost, while _seen() keeps the site 'online'. 4) There is no route or edge_id to reset the stream. 5) Capabilities: 'latest' is chosen by ORDER BY seq DESC (routes_edge.py:425), so after a reset the old capabilities stay current. sites.set_tier_capable still takes any message, including a late, older retry. Acks have no idempotency and are stored again on every retry.
expected: Data is never lost silently. Idempotency should be by (site, edge, stream, seq) with a set of seen sequences or a window, not a single high-water mark. A capabilities or boot message (U3: the edge sends it on boot) or an edge_id change should start a new sequence epoch. A batch below the mark that was never stored should be stored, or at least refused rather than acknowledged.
actual: An out-of-order or reset sequence is acknowledged as a duplicate. The edge purges, and telemetry and safety events are lost without any error. It also suppresses the pause on readback_mismatch, local_override and template_change.
evidence: routes_edge.py:83-92, 277-278, 327-332 and 425. telemetry.py:622-630. U3 5.2: 'the cloud acknowledges by seq so the edge can purge its store'.

title: The slot-count reduction never re-merges adjacent same-mode runs, so planned charging is dropped or slots are wasted (Sungrow 2, Growatt 3)
label: bug
steps: 1) Same-mode neighbours are coalesced only once, before the max_slots loop (152-157). Inside 'while len(runs) > max_slots' (158-160), merge() can leave two adjacent runs with the same mode, and they are never coalesced. 2) A run that is not discharging, with two discharging neighbours, falls back to `or cands` and folds into the higher-energy discharge. That is the mirror of the DESIGN_LOG case. 3) Probe day: charge_grid 00-02 (10 kW), discharge 02-06 (5 kW), charge_grid 06-07 (5 kW), discharge 07-24 (10 kW).
expected: After each merge, adjacent runs with equal mode are coalesced before another boundary is dropped. Sungrow should give [charge_grid 00:00-02:00, discharge 02:00-24:00]; Growatt should give [charge_grid, discharge] in 2 slots.
actual: Sungrow gives [('00:00','06:00','discharge'), ('06:00','00:00','discharge')]: all the planned grid charging is gone and the day is one discharge split in two. Growatt gives [charge_grid 00-02, discharge 02-06, discharge 06-24], wasting a slot. The twin replays and the vendor view then show a table that never charges.
evidence: Probe output (scratchpad probe4.py): 'sungrow [('00:00', '06:00', 'discharge'), ('06:00', '00:00', 'discharge')]' and 'growatt [('00:00','02:00','charge_grid'), ('02:00','06:00','discharge'), ('06:00','00:00','discharge')]'. delivery.py:125-160.

title: The Huawei vendor view gives periods Huawei rejects (end 00:00, a 00:00-00:00 full day) and a 'hold' type it does not have, with no SoC targets
label: spec-mismatch
steps: 1) vendor_view for huawei (223-225) sets end = strftime of s1.t+900, so a day's last period ends at '00:00'. A full-day slot reads start '00:00', end '00:00'. The scratch Lahore mall plan has a 2026-11-10 period 00:00 to 00:00. 2) charge_or_discharge maps every slot that is not charge, discharge or export (hold, self_use) to 'hold'. 3) The row carries no SoC: no global grid-charge cut-off (47088, the maximum of the grid-charge targets), no discharge floor or backup SoC, and no capacity-control (MDI) periods, although BRANDS['huawei'].mdi_primitive is True. 4) The frontend vendor-table.tsx shows these rows verbatim as 'The table to key in'.
expected: R6 3.2 and U3 2.4: periods have 0 <= start < end <= 1440 and the last period ends at 23:59, not 00:00. A period is charge (0) or discharge (1); 'hold' is expressed by leaving the time out (the battery does not discharge outside set periods), and self_use should be a discharge period. Part 7.1 step 4 translates targets: a global grid-charge cut-off at the maximum of the grid-charge targets, floors through 47082 and 47102, and mdi_cap_kw through the capacity-control periods.
actual: An installer keying the table gets an 'unknown error' or rejection on the end-00:00 period, has no way to enter 'hold', and is given no SoC target. A grid-charge period then charges to whatever cut-off is already set.
evidence: delivery.py:223-225. Scratch plan: Lahore mall slots include ('2026-11-10','00:00','00:00','hold',95.0,...). Probe: huawei [{'period':1,'start':'18:00','end':'20:00',...},{'period':2,'start':'20:00','end':'00:00','charge_or_discharge':'hold'}]. R6 3.2: 'end the last period at 23:59 not 00:00'.

title: Growatt, Sungrow, Voltronic and Solis are compiled as N contiguous slots of any mode and shown in a generic view; Growatt's 3+3 windows and global SoC are not modelled
label: spec-mismatch
steps: 1) BRANDS['growatt'] has max_slots 3, so the whole day, self-use included, is squeezed into 3 contiguous slots. 2) vendor_view (226-227) gives every non-Deye, non-Huawei brand rows of {slot, start, end, mode, soc_pct} in the Mode A vocabulary (hold, charge_grid, self_use, ...), with a per-slot soc_pct. 3) The grammar fields (enabled, target_soc, current_a, mode) are never produced. table_writes_per_day, ring and fields are unused by the compiler (only the control page shows them).
expected: Growatt: up to 3 Battery-First windows plus 3 Grid-First windows (9 on TL-XH), with the rest of the day Load First, so self-use runs need no slot. Charge stop SoC (1091), AC charge (1092) and grid-first min SoC (1071) are global. Sungrow: Max and Min SoC plus two forced-charge windows with a target SoC. Voltronic: POP and PCP changes with voltage thresholds. Solis: 3 charge and 3 discharge windows with a current. DLV-02 asks for a per-brand rendering of each.
actual: The compiler drops boundaries Growatt could have kept, because self-use counts against 3. It then shows per-window SoC values Growatt cannot hold per window, and mode names ('hold', 'charge_grid') that are not Growatt, Sungrow or Voltronic settings. The installer has to translate them by hand, and the twin replays semantics the device lacks.
evidence: delivery.py:33-42 (BRANDS), 158 (the max_slots cap), 226-227 (generic rows). Probe: growatt [{'slot':1,...,'mode':'discharge','soc_pct':50},{'slot':2,...,'mode':'self_use','soc_pct':50}]. R6 3.4: 'Mode A on Growatt: up to 3 Battery-First windows ... and up to 3 Grid-First windows ...; the rest of the day is Load First. No per-window power or SoC.'

title: The Deye vendor view keys self-use slots as power 0 (no discharge) while the twin runs them unlimited; it has no 'sell' flag and no peak-shaving value
label: spec-mismatch
steps: 1) The Deye row sets power_w = max_discharge_w or max_charge_w or 0. max_discharge_w is set only for discharge and export slots (185), so every self_use slot is keyed with power 0, which on Deye is the slot's maximum discharge, i.e. a hold. twin.slots_policy treats max_discharge_w None as unlimited. Scratch textile plan on 2026-11-08: program 1 is 12:00 self_use (8 grid-up steps), keyed with power_w 0 and soc 78. 2) There is no 'sell' bit (export_allowed), so an export slot keyed on Deye does not export. 3) grid_cap_w (which the twin uses to peak-shave) is not shown, although Deye's grid peak-shaving registers 280 and 292-293 exist (R6 3.1). 4) Days with fewer than 6 slots give fewer than 6 rows, and Deye has 6 ring programs that must all be filled.
expected: Deye rows that reproduce what the twin replays and the plan assumes: self_use keyed with power at rated or the slot's planned maximum; the sell flag for export slots; a peak-shaving value where the MDI cap is meant to bind, or mdi_not_enforceable reported (Part 7.1 step 4); unused programs filled in so the ring is defined.
actual: What the installer keys into a Deye differs from what the twin replays: self-use is held and export never sells. The demo and plan_compare credit behaviour the keyed table does not produce.
evidence: delivery.py:185 and 220-222. twin.py:208-209. Scratch probe7.py: [{'program':1,'time':'12:00','power_w':0,'soc_pct':78,...}] for slot ('12:00','self_use',None,78.3). U3 2.4: the Deye sell bit lives in the flags register.

title: No whole-table safety (I1 safe tail): a table that persists on Deye or Growatt is never checked, and only today's remainder is compiled as day 0
label: spec-mismatch
area: Mode A compiler (Part 7.1 step 6, R6 I1/I5)
steps: 1) compile_mode_a groups the 192 steps by local date. Day 0 starts at the tick's quarter (for example 12:15) and the third day is partial. 2) Nothing checks that the last slot's floor equals max(reserve, fallback floor), that the twin-replayed SoC stays at or above the reserve up to valid_until, or that tomorrow's table is safe on its own as a fallback day. 3) The Control page defaults to today's table (vendor-table.tsx picks pktToday), which on a Deye ring starts at the tick time, so its last program wraps through to the same time tomorrow. 4) Example tails from the scratch demo: the feed mill's last slot is 'hold' with floor 20 (the fallback, not the reserve). A tail that is charge_grid, discharge or export would be repeated indefinitely on a slot-only brand with no edge.
expected: Part 7.1 step 6: two day-tables (today's remainder and tomorrow), each safe to repeat. The last slot's floor equals the larger of the reserve and the fallback floor, and the replayed SoC stays at or above the reserve for the next known or likely window; a table that fails is not signed.
actual: There is no safe-tail check. A table keyed by an installer, or left in place after link loss or expiry on Deye or Growatt, repeats whatever the last slot holds, with nothing proving it is safe.
evidence: delivery.py:105-200 (no tail logic). plans.py:446-449 (only _guard runs, and it is vacuous). R6 4.1 I1: 'the final slot's floor must equal max(reserve.min_soc_pct, fallback.min_soc_floor_pct)'.

title: No write budget or nightly table: every 15-minute plan is a new table, and 'Table writes today' counts edge pulls on a UTC date
label: spec-mismatch
steps: 1) Each tick (every 15 minutes) stores a new plan with a newly compiled table, and signed_message serves it. There is no nightly table after the 23:00 solve, no rule for an event rewrite (gain > Rs 500, budget left, at least 60 minutes since the last write), and no write_budget or apply_policy in the message. 2) /control's budget.used_today is COUNT(*) of plan_messages for the day, and a row is written on every key pull of /plans/current/message (plans._record_send), including repeat pulls of the same plan. An edge polling every minute shows '1440 of 3'. 3) It compares substr(sent_at,1,10) (store._now(), a UTC ISO date) with today() (the Pakistan date), so between 00:00 and 05:00 PKT it counts the previous UTC day. 4) Frontend capabilities-card.tsx:19-31 shows 'Table writes today N of 3' and, when full, 'Today's budget is used: the next table goes out tomorrow unless a hold or release needs it'. Nothing holds the next table back. 5) Each pull also stores the full message body, so storage grows without bound.
expected: The cloud uses at most 3 table writes a day against the edge cap of 4: the nightly table, then event rewrites only when they pass the gain and spacing rules. The message carries apply_policy and write_budget. The meter counts table changes actually written (from acks' writes_used_today) by local day. For tier 2 there is a stable daily table to key in.
actual: With an edge that writes on change, the 4 a day EEPROM budget is gone by about 01:00 and the rest of the day runs whichever table landed first. A tier-2 installer sees a table that changes every 15 minutes. The budget card counts pulls and claims a hold-back that does not exist.
evidence: routes_plans.py:141-147. plans.py:669-673 and 711-713 (a record on every pull). routes_edge.py:408-417. delivery.py:28-43 (table_writes_per_day is never used by the compiler). frontend/src/features/devices/capabilities-card.tsx:19-31.

title: The heartbeat reports clock-offset actions ('control demoted', 'peak slots widened') that the code never takes
label: spec-mismatch
area: edge heartbeat / clock drift (R6 C10, Part 7.3)
steps: 1) POST /api/edge/{id}/heartbeat with clock_offset_s 1000. 2) The answer is warning 'clock_offset_900s: control demoted until the clock is set'. 3) Check the site: tier and tier_allowed are unchanged, no override is written, no alert is raised, and compile_mode_a has no widening logic. A grep for clock_offset finds only this handler and the model. 4) At 300 s the answer says 'peak slots are widened by 15 minutes', and nothing is widened. There is no warning at 120 s.
expected: R6 C10 and Part 7.3: over 120 s raise clock_unsynced. Over 300 s the compiler starts every peak-avoidance or discharge slot 15 minutes early and ends it 15 minutes late, and the installer is asked to set the clock. Over 900 s the site is demoted to advisory until the offset is under 120 s.
actual: The heartbeat is stored in site_state and nothing reads clock_offset_s. A site whose inverter clock is 20 minutes off stays closed_loop, with slot boundaries shifted into the peak, and the edge is told control was demoted.
evidence: routes_edge.py:295-306. A grep across gridlytics/*.py for 'clock_offset' returns only routes_edge.py:302-305 and delivery.py:320.

title: The ems-edge/1.0 models refuse U3's own contract: envelope fields, event names, partial acks, heartbeat states and the telemetry shape
label: spec-mismatch
steps: Validate U3 section 5 examples against the models (probe3.py): (a) an events batch with U3's envelope (msg_type, msg_id, site_id, edge_id) and a per-event 'source' gets 422 extra_forbidden; (b) event type 'override_local' (U3's name; the model has 'local_override') gets a literal_error, and so do template_change_detected, firmware_change_detected, edge_reboot and installer_session_start/end; (c) ack status 'partial' and the per_device shape are refused; (d) heartbeat control_state 'executing' or 'fallback' is refused; (e) telemetry 'data', 'interval_s', 'ts_start', 'aggregation' and 'sample_period_s' are refused, and 'rows' is required. One unknown event type refuses the whole batch with 422, outage_start included, and the docstring says the edge drops a 422 batch. The plan message has no supersedes, capabilities_seq, targets or msg_id, and no pydantic model validates it or checks it against stored capabilities (R6 C1). There are no contract tests (backend/tests/contract is missing) and no exported schema files. The DESIGN_LOG records none of these deviations.
expected: DAT-02: 'Every example in U3 section 5 validates.' DAT-03: an envelope site_id that differs from the key's site is refused with 403. U3 5.4: the plan carries supersedes and capabilities_seq (CAPS_STALE). Unknown optional event types should not void a batch under 1.x semantic versioning.
actual: A Product 2 edge or partner gateway built to the documented contract is refused on every message type. A single new event type loses the batch's outage and pause events.
evidence: Probe: 'U3 events envelope REFUSED: [events.0.source extra_forbidden, msg_type ..., msg_id ..., site_id ..., edge_id ...]', 'events ... U3 type names REFUSED: [events.0.type literal_error]', 'ack partial REFUSED', 'heartbeat U3 state REFUSED', 'telemetry U3 shape REFUSED: rows missing, data extra_forbidden, interval_s extra_forbidden'. delivery.py:301-357. plans.py:704-710.

title: What the edge reports is stored but never acted on: rejected or partial acks, control_disabled, firmware_change and heartbeat control_state
label: feature-gap
area: edge escalation rules (R6 C5, C6, C8; Part 7.3)
steps: 1) PAUSE_EVENTS = readback_mismatch, local_override and template_change. firmware_change and control_disabled do not pause or demote. 2) /ack stores rows, and nothing reads status 'rejected' or 'expired' or the items' 'clamped' or 'failed' (C5: re-plan with the achieved values). 3) A heartbeat with control_state 'native' or 'disabled' is stored in site_state.edge_heartbeat only. 4) routes_sites.control_state (31-52) returns 'Following plan' for closed_loop whenever telemetry is fresh, and verify.compute_day (718-719) classes every closed_loop day 'confirmed' by construction. So a site whose edge rejected the plan or fell back to native shows 'Following plan', and its savings count as confirmed.
expected: C8: a template or firmware change moves the site to advisory and recompiles. C5: partial or rejected acks re-enter the optimiser and the UI. C6: unknown state leads to a re-plan, and two mismatches in 24 h demote. Control state and fidelity at closed-loop sites come from acks, heartbeats and fallback events, not 'by construction'.
actual: After a firmware change the cloud keeps signing plans for a register map that may have changed. Rejected plans, fallback and edge-disabled control are invisible on the control page and in the fidelity class.
evidence: routes_edge.py:38, 338-339 and 375-384. routes_sites.py:43-52. verify.py:718-719 ('elif site.get("demo_link") or tier == "closed_loop": fidelity = "confirmed"'). A grep finds no reader of the acks table except the edge_status listing.

title: The signing key is found by an absolute file path and silently replaced when the file is missing; keys are not in backups
label: bug
steps: 1) _site_key reads site_keys.private_path, an absolute path built from data_dir() when the key was made. If Path(private_path).exists() is False, it generates a new key, inserts a second unretired row, and returns it, with no audit line and no warning. 2) Move the data folder (Windows C:\... to the Linux or Docker host the HANDOFF plans for), or restore companies/*.db onto a new machine. backups.py copies only *.db files, never data/keys. 3) The next plan pull is signed with a new key, and every edge provisioned with the old public key rejects every plan (SIG_INVALID) with no cloud-side signal. 4) Two concurrent first calls can each mint a key. Both rows stay active, with ORDER BY created DESC on second resolution, so which key signs is not deterministic. 5) There is no rotate_key command, and 'retired' is never set.
expected: Part 2.8: keys are kept with the data folder's secrets, provisioned to the edge, rotated by a signed rotate_key command and on handover. The off-machine backup carries the secrets (encrypted), and the restore drill proves signing works after a restore. A missing key is an error that needs action, not a silent rotation.
actual: Signing breaks silently after a folder move or restore, and the public key the page shows changes without notice.
evidence: delivery.py:248-272 (Path(r['private_path']).exists() else generate). backups.py:77-107 (only .db files). store.py:200 (site_keys table).

title: The Mode A fallback block carries a 3-hour revert timer the spec forbids, and the UI promises an automatic revert that a keyed table never does
label: spec-mismatch
area: plan expiry / fallback (Part 7.1 step 6, U3 3.4, R6 I1-I6)
steps: 1) compile_mode_a's fallback is {on_expiry: inverter_native, min_soc_floor_pct: reserve_policy.min_soc_pct, revert_after_hours: 3}. 2) The signed plan carries it unchanged, with valid_until 48 h later, so the message is self-contradictory. 3) It lacks max_export_w_floor, native_settings_ref and on_link_loss_after_s. min_soc_floor_pct is not max(BMS low+2, backup reserve, 10) (I2), so min_soc_pct 5 gives a fallback floor of 5 while the slots are clamped to 12. 4) The release message's valid_until is the override's end, which is 7 days for an edge-triggered pause (_pause_in) and up to 72 h from the control page, beyond the 48 h limit. 5) Frontend slot-words.ts:26 tells the user: 'If the plan expires, or no fresh plan arrives for 3 hours, the inverter returns to its native settings'. On a tier-2 Deye or Growatt the keyed table persists indefinitely and nothing reverts.
expected: Part 7.1 step 6 and DLV-03: the Mode A fallback block carries on_expiry, min_soc_floor_pct, max_export_w_floor and native_settings_ref, and no revert timer; the 1,800 s revert belongs to Mode B. I6: on link loss the edge keeps the cached plan to valid_until. Every message's valid_until is at most 48 h after issue.
actual: An edge cannot tell whether to revert after 3 h or run to 48 h. An installer or owner is told the inverter reverts by itself when it does not. The fallback carries no export floor or native reference.
evidence: delivery.py:199-200. plans.py:682-686 (release valid_until = rel['until']). routes_edge.py:312 (7-day pause). frontend/src/features/plan/slot-words.ts:24-27. Scratch plans: fallback {'on_expiry':'inverter_native','min_soc_floor_pct':20.0,'revert_after_hours':3}.

title: The twin peak-shaves every brand to grid_cap_w, below the slot floor and the outage reserve; the demo credits MDI and peak cuts the devices cannot make
label: spec-mismatch
area: twin realism / Mode A MDI translation (Part 7.1 step 4)
steps: 1) compile_mode_a puts grid_cap_w (the MDI cap) on every slot (193-194). DESIGN_LOG 2026-11-06 says 'every slot carries grid_cap_w so the device peak-shaves to it'. 2) twin.simulate (348-351) discharges in any mode, hold and charge_grid included, to keep import at or below gcap, down to dis_room_abs (the BMS floor e_min), ignoring the slot floor and reserve. 3) Scratch feed-mill telemetry with the grid up: 627 kWh discharged in 'charge_grid' minutes and 191.5 kWh in 'hold' minutes, with min SoC 10 % in both, against slot floors of 20 % or more. 4) Spec: Deye, Growatt and Sungrow have no peak-shaving primitive in Mode A, the floor wins, and the plan reports mdi_not_enforceable. The Deye vendor view never shows a cap. Native replays have no gcap, so the plan arm alone gets the capability.
expected: The twin executes only what the brand's grammar (or the tier-2 vendor view) can carry. On brands without an MDI primitive the cap becomes max_discharge_w and floors, the floor wins, and mdi_not_enforceable is reported. No shaving below the slot floor or reserve.
actual: Demo savings (the MDI and peak levers), plan_compare and the guard replay assume peak shaving that a keyed Deye, Growatt or Sungrow table cannot do. In the twin, shaving drains a held outage reserve to the BMS floor.
evidence: twin.py:348-351. delivery.py:191-194. Probe6 telemetry: "Karachi feed mill [('charge_grid', 11047, 626.9, 10.0), ('discharge', 945, 1872.0, 13.52), ('hold', 5871, 191.5, 10.0), ...]". A grep for mdi_not_enforceable finds nothing.

title: The native replay ignores the captured slot's max_charge_kw: the baseline grid-charges at full battery power
label: bug
steps: 1) NativeCapture slots accept max_charge_kw (sites.py:415). 2) twin.native_policy returns max_ch = inf for every minute (192) and never reads it, nor any discharge power limit. 3) verify.compute_day (700-701) prices the native arm from this policy. Example: a Deye native table that grid-charges 01:00-05:00 at 10 kW on a 100 kW battery is replayed at 100 kW, ten times faster.
expected: Part 7.4: the twin models the inverter's native mode with its configured slots and targets so the baseline is realistic, including the captured charge power.
actual: The baseline's grid charging is faster than the site's real settings, so its import power and monthly MDI peak are inflated. The MDI lever (and the timing of off-peak energy) is then over-credited to the plan at any site whose native capture has power-limited grid-charge slots.
evidence: sites.py:409-415 (NativeSlot.max_charge_kw). twin.py:156-193 ('max_ch': np.full(n, np.inf)). A grep shows max_charge_kw used nowhere else.

title: Mode B is never executed by the twin: Mode B sites (the feed mill) run the 2-slot Mode A table in the demo, the guard and plan_compare
label: feature-gap
steps: 1) The Karachi feed mill has control_mode mode_b, and its plans are stored with mode 'b'. The signed message carries mode_b.steps. 2) demo._policy_for (161-178) always builds twin.slots_policy from the Mode A slots. plans._guard (338) and routes_plans.plan_compare (120) do the same. So the site's demo telemetry and savings come from the Sungrow 2-slot table, not the per-step setpoints the edge would follow. 3) mode_b() also leaves out battery_mode, soc_target_pct, export_limit_w and gen_charge_allowed, and genset_request is a bool rather than U3's enum (none, prefer_start, prefer_stop). Its floors are not clamped (see the floor finding).
expected: DLV-06: Mode B schedule and refresh block, validated against the twin. Part 7.2: 192 step objects of the abstract primitives. The twin executes per-step battery_power_w within the residual band.
actual: Mode B is published but never simulated or checked. The demo's closed-loop Mode B savings are those of a 2-slot emulation, and the Mode B message is never replayed before signing.
evidence: demo.py:166-167. plans.py:338. routes_plans.py:120. delivery.py:240-243. Scratch: the feed mill plan has mode 'b', brand sungrow, and 5 compiled slots that drive the twin.

title: The demo applies every 3-hourly (live: 15-minute) plan instantly at advisory_writes sites and counts it 'confirmed', overstating what tier 2 achieves
label: spec-mismatch
steps: 1) The textile mill (Deye) and the farm (Voltronic) are tier advisory_writes. 2) _policy_for runs the plan's slots for every tier except monitor, and _replanned_span re-plans every 3 hours (round 5) while advance() follows plans.current every 15 minutes. So the twin re-keys the table 8 to 96 times a day. 3) verify.compute_day (718-719) sets fidelity 'confirmed' for any demo_link site, and routes_sites.control_state says 'Following plan (table applied)'.
expected: Tier 2 means a person keys a daily table through the vendor app, at most a few writes a day (Part 7.1 step 7), confirmed from telemetry (7.6). A demo of an advisory site should apply one table a day (for example the 23:00 nightly table) and score its fidelity.
actual: The demo's advisory-site savings are closed-loop savings with many writes a day. Customers shown the demo see what tier 2 cannot deliver. The DESIGN_LOG chose re-planning every 3 hours 'as live ticks re-plan every 15 minutes', without excluding advisory sites.
evidence: demo.py:161-178 and 250-259. verify.py:718-719. DESIGN_LOG round 5: 'The demo history re-plans every 3 hours'.

title: charge_end_ts is not enforced anywhere: the twin keeps a charge slot charging past its 'charge end', into the hours the plan kept free
label: bug
area: Mode A charge slot end (HANDOFF 8.A.4, round 4)
steps: 1) compile_mode_a sets charge_end_ts at the last planned charge step and computes max_charge_w as the mean up to it. The code comment says it 'ends the charge there'. 2) twin.slots_policy never reads charge_end_ts: the slot stays mode charge_grid until end_ts, and twin.simulate (333-334) grid-charges at max_ch until the target. 3) When the gcap (MDI cap) or the load holds the charge back (charge_grid: bat <= gcap - net), the charge falls behind and runs on past charge_end into the peak. The Deye and Huawei vendor views have no charge-end boundary either. 4) The frontend shows 'charges until HH:MM' (slot-words.ts) as if it were enforced.
expected: The charge stops at charge_end_ts: either a real slot boundary (a hold slot from charge_end), or the twin and edge treat charge_end_ts as the end of grid charging.
actual: charge_end is informational only. Execution can grid-charge after it, into peak hours, which the round 4 fix was meant to prevent.
evidence: delivery.py:171-190. twin.py:196-217 (no charge_end_ts) and 333-334. frontend/src/features/plan/slot-words.ts (the charge_end sentence).

title: The twin's export mode discharges at a fixed cap and books the battery energy above the export cap as curtailed PV, even at night
label: bug
steps: 1) In mode 5 (export) the battery discharges min(pdis, dis_room) whatever the load or export cap. 2) Anything beyond x_max becomes 'curtail' (359-362), and out['pv'] = max(0, pv - curtail) (446). 3) Probe: x_max 20 kW, 10 kW load, no PV, an export slot at 100 kW for 60 minutes. The battery gives 100 kWh, export is 20 kWh, the load takes 10 kWh, and 70 kWh is 'curtailed' with PV 0.
expected: Export discharge is limited to load plus export cap (an inverter does not discharge into curtailment), and the energy balance closes within 1 W (TWN-01).
actual: Battery energy disappears into 'curtailment', breaking the balance and the curtail KPI whenever actual load or PV differs from the forecast behind max_discharge_w (the maximum over the slot). It affects net-billing sites' plan_compare, guard and demo.
evidence: Probe output (scratchpad probe1.py): 'export test: bat kWh 100.0 exp kWh 20.0 load kWh 10 curtail kWh 70.0 pv 0.0'. twin.py:337-338, 359-362 and 446.

title: The twin has no brand profiles (TWN-02): native and Mode A replays use one generic inverter for every brand
label: feature-gap
steps: native_policy and slots_policy are brand-agnostic. Brand semantics R6 4.6 names are not modelled: Huawei does not discharge outside set periods; Growatt runs Load First outside windows with global SoC limits; Deye stops following programs at BATTERY_LOW_CAP and charges from PV above the slot capacity; Voltronic works on voltage thresholds. Minutes outside any slot always run self_use with a 20 % floor (slots_policy:199). In hold and charge_pv_only slots the twin caps PV charging at the slot target, so at zero-export sites PV is curtailed where Deye would store it.
expected: TWN-02: brand profiles (from DLV-00) with slot grammar, primitives, budgets and quirks, so native replays and table replays reflect each brand.
actual: Savings replays and guard replays rest on one generic logic. For each brand they can differ from what the inverter does, in both directions.
evidence: twin.py:156-217 (no brand input). delivery.BRANDS is not used by the twin. EMS_BUILD_PROGRESS items TWN-02 and DLV-00 (JSON brand files).

title: The canonical JSON for signatures is Python's json.dumps, which a non-Python edge cannot reproduce for floats
label: bug
steps: canonical() = json.dumps(sort_keys, separators, default=str). The plan is sent as parsed JSON, not as the signed bytes, so the verifier must re-serialise. Python writes 20.0 and 1e-05, while JavaScript's JSON.stringify writes 20 and 0.00001. Plan bodies are full of floats (soc_floor_pct 20.0, min_soc_floor_pct 20.0). A Go or JavaScript edge re-canonicalising gets different bytes and rejects the plan with SIG_INVALID.
expected: A language-neutral canonical form (RFC 8785 JCS), or a detached signature over the exact transmitted bytes (for example a base64 payload plus sig).
actual: Only a Python verifier with identical json settings can check signatures.
evidence: delivery.py:281-296. U3 5.1: 'sig (Ed25519 signature over the canonical JSON of the body, base64)'.

title: Edge messages accept unbounded free-form dicts and strings up to the 25 MB API cap, and the heartbeat body is written into the site's carried state
label: bug
steps: Heartbeat fields active_plan, valid_until and sent_at have no max_length. Event.detail, TelemetryBatch.quality and Capabilities.devices are free-form dicts (delivery.py:305-357). api.MAX_BODY is 25,000,000 for every /api path. A site key can send a 20 MB heartbeat, which _put_state(edge_heartbeat=...) stores in site_state, read on every tick and page. 500 events with large details are stored in the events table.
expected: DAT-03: a 1 MiB cap on edge ingest, and bounded string and dict fields in the strict contract models.
actual: One site key can bloat the workspace file and slow every tick and page for that site.
evidence: routes_edge.py:295-306. delivery.py:305-357. api.py:100 (MAX_BODY = 25_000_000).

title: plans.current and the signed message ignore valid_until: an expired plan stays 'active' and is served to the edge
label: bug
steps: plans.current selects status='active' with no time check. If ticks stop (the site is not 'active', the scheduler is off, or 48 h of failed solves, since a failed tick keeps the previous plan active), signed_message keeps signing and serving a plan whose valid_until has passed and records a 'send'. The control page shows its table as the one to key in.
expected: Part 2.4: failed(reason) keeps the previous plan active until its valid_until; after that no plan is in force, and the page shows the site in fallback (R6 4.4 'site in fallback' alert).
actual: A stale plan is presented and served indefinitely. Only an edge that checks expiry protects the site.
evidence: plans.py:521-530 (current) and 694-714. There is no valid_until comparison on read.

title: GET /api/sites/{id}/events returns fuel-log cost_rs to a viewer and to any sites:read API key (money filter skipped)
label: bug
steps:
1) As an operator: POST /api/sites/{sid}/genset/fuel {"litres":50,"day":"2026-11-05","cost_rs":14000,"note":"tanker"}. This stores an events row of type 'fuel_log' whose detail is {day, litres, note, cost_rs} (routes_telemetry.py:390-395).
2) As the viewer (Authorization: Bearer <viewer token>): GET /api/sites/{sid}/events.
3) Or with a site key that holds only sites:read: GET /api/sites/{sid}/events with Authorization: Bearer glk_.... The guard maps the path to resource 'sites' and scope sites:read (apikeys.py:42-43) and lets it through.
expected:
No money for a viewer or for any machine key. The route should go through routes_common.out(), as GET /api/sites/{id}/genset/fuel does (routes_telemetry.py:370, which strips cost_rs for a viewer).
Sources: DESIGN_LOG 'Money on the wire'; plan Part 2.8 ('a viewer never sees the fuel price, the fee or the company's cost settings'); plan Part 10.5 (keys carry no money); HANDOFF section 4 (for_reader strips for a viewer and for every key).
actual: The route returns [{...row, "detail": json.loads(detail)}] raw (lines 190-192). The answer includes {"type":"fuel_log","detail":{"litres":50,"cost_rs":14000,...},"source":"<operator's name>"} for every role and for a partner or edge key. No web page renders /events today, so the leak is reachable through the API with any member's token or a sites:read key.
evidence:
routes_telemetry.py:187-192: events() has no out() and no auth.need.
routes_telemetry.py:373-396: the fuel log stores cost_rs in events.detail.
routes_telemetry.py:355-370: fuel_logs() reads the same rows and wraps them in out().
test_fix_r3_api.py:431-441 asserts the viewer has no cost_rs only on /genset/fuel.
test_api_walk.py:61-71 (test_the_viewer_gets_no_rupees) greps just 5 routes (plan, fleet, savings, genset, site), so /events was never checked, although PAGES at line 47 fetches it with a 200 check only.

title: The money filter is opt-in per route (out()) and matches key names; about 20 member-readable GET routes skip it, and the role-walk test covers 5 routes
label: spec-mismatch
steps:
List the GET routes that return without out() and without auth.need:
- /api/sites/{id}/events
- /native
- /overrides
- /pilot
- /outages
- /forecasts/{kind} and /forecasts/scores
- /telemetry, /telemetry/days, /telemetry/heatmap, /telemetry/quality
- /plan (held branch, routes_plans.py:29-34)
- /api/alerts/counts and /api/alerts/rules
- /api/reports
- /api/demo
- /api/drafts

Any money key added later to telemetry.days, forecast.page, the outage log, the pilot body or an edge event's detail reaches viewers and keys unfiltered. The events leak above is the first instance.
expected: Plan Part 10.5: 'The viewer filter is server-side and typed, not a key grep: every money field in every response model is annotated Money ... test_role_walk.py compares the admin's and the viewer's answer to every route and fails on any shared money value.' At minimum, the filter should be applied to every JSON answer centrally (a response class or middleware keyed on auth.current), so a route cannot forget it, and the walk should diff admin against viewer on every GET in PAGES.
actual: The filter runs only where a route calls out() (money.py:45-52, routes_common.py:55-58). DESIGN_LOG 'Money on the wire' records the key-name grep as the implementation, but the 'every route' walk was not built: the viewer test checks 5 routes against 9 fixed key names (test_api_walk.py:61-71).
evidence: An AST scan of routes_*.py lists 20+ GET routes without out(). money.py:24-26: is_money is name-based only. test_api_walk.py:61-71 checks only 5 routes. No file named test_role_walk.py exists.

title: Viewer receives every alert category (Tariff, Control, Savings, Genset requests); the plan limits a viewer to energy-category alerts
label: spec-mismatch
expected: Plan Part 10.5: 'a viewer gets 404 on money kinds and only energy-category alerts'. A viewer's listing and counts should be filtered to the energy categories (Data, Reserve, Battery, Forecast, and Genset if judged energy). Neither DESIGN_LOG nor HANDOFF records a deviation.
actual: inbox() returns out(alerts.listing(state, site_id, category)) with no role filter (routes_alerts.py:14-15). alerts.listing selects all categories (alerts.py:297-315). counts() counts all of them (routes_alerts.py:19-22). The money keys inside detail are stripped, but the categories are not restricted.
evidence: routes_alerts.py:13-22; alerts.py:19 (CATEGORIES includes Tariff, Savings and Control); alerts.py:164 (Tariff alert); routes_sites.py:423.

title: Mutating routes without an audit row, and audit rows without before/after values for money settings
label: spec-mismatch
expected: Plan Part 2.8: 'Every mutating route is audited (who, why, before, after): overrides, tariff edits, settings, applied records, captures, calendar locks, resumes, acks, report generation and exports; test_audit_walk.py holds every mutating route to an audit row.'
actual: Several mutating routes write no audit line. The money settings that price the optimiser and the ledger are audited without before or after values, so a change of a battery price, VoLL or genset costs cannot be reconstructed. There is no test_audit_walk.py in backend/tests.
evidence: grep 'store.audit' finds no call in pilot_put, recompute, fuel_log, outage_cause, forecasts.refresh or set_tier_capable. sites.py:245 and sites.py:320 show the value-less audit details. The audit test file does not exist.

title: PUT /pilot can rewrite the pilot's sign-off after it started and can seed a fake amendments history before it starts; the values are unvalidated and the change is not audited
label: bug
steps:
1) As the admin, POST /api/sites/{sid}/pilot/start {"name":"Plant manager"}. The stored signoff is {by: <admin>, at, name}.
2) PUT /api/sites/{sid}/pilot {"signoff":{"by":"Customer CEO","at":"2026-10-01T00:00:00+00:00","name":"CEO"}}.
3) GET /api/sites/{sid}/pilot. The signoff now reads Customer CEO; the only trace is an amendment {changes:["signoff"]} with no old value.
4) Before the start, PUT {"amendments":[{...invented history...}],"criteria":"x"} is stored as sent.
expected: The pilot's sign-off is written only by POST /pilot/start and is immutable afterwards. PUT should accept only baseline_start, baseline_days and criteria, validate their types, and record before and after in the audit (plan Part 2.8). After the start, amendments should record the old and new values.
actual: data = {**cur['pilot'], **{k: v for k in inp if k in PILOT_DEFAULT}} (line 150). PILOT_DEFAULT includes 'signoff' and 'amendments' (lines 131-133), so both are writable. Values are not type-checked, and store.audit is never called.
evidence: routes_savings.py:131-133 (PILOT_DEFAULT keys), 145-156 (pilot_put), 159-174 (pilot_start writes the signoff).

title: Switchback calendar can be backdated and re-rolled with a predictable seed, which clears 'Preliminary' and lets someone choose arm labels after seeing the costs
label: bug
steps:
As an operator (edit_sites), at a site with 28+ verified days and a native capture, whose FCA months are billed:
1) PUT /api/sites/{sid}/switchback {"start":"2026-08-01","fortnights":4,"block_days":7}. The start in the past is accepted (routes_savings.py:85-93 checks only the counts).
2) GET /api/sites/{sid}/savings. In verify.summary, sb_days counts blocks whose block_end is before today (verify.py:1095-1096), so the 8 switchback weeks are met at once and preliminary turns false without any switchback having run.
3) Repaint as often as wanted; arms come from np.random.default_rng(int(datetime.now().timestamp())) (verify.py:1127), so the arms for any second are computable in advance. Labels can be picked so that native-labelled past days are the costly ones; switchback_result (verify.py:1190-1230) then reports the chosen saving_rs_per_day.
4) The audit line records start and fortnights but not the drawn arms (verify.py:1142).
actual: Any operator can produce a backdated, cherry-picked calendar that removes the Preliminary label from customer savings and reports and sets the switchback figure. Separately, live ticks never consult the calendar (arm_on is used only by demo.py:162), so even a forward calendar's 'native' blocks still run the plan at real sites.
evidence: routes_savings.py:80-94; verify.py:1125-1143 (paint, timestamp seed, unlocked repaint); verify.py:1093-1099 (preliminary uses sb_days); verify.py:711-716 (native_block labels by calendar); `grep -rn arm_on` finds it only in demo.py and verify.py.

title: API key scopes: sites:read reaches the current plan and every GET under the site, while plans:read gates only /plans; the edge/partner key kind is not enforced
label: spec-mismatch
steps:
1) As the admin: POST /api/platform/keys {"name":"p","scopes":["sites:read"],"site_id":S,"kind":"partner"}.
2) With that key: GET /api/sites/S/plan returns 200 with the full current plan (money stripped), and GET /api/sites/S/plans returns 403 out_of_scope.
3) The same key reads /telemetry (1-minute data), /control, /plan/compare, /savings (energy), /events, /pilot, /outages and /forecasts/*.
4) POST /api/platform/keys {...,"kind":"partner","scopes":["telemetry:write"]} is accepted, and that partner key can POST /api/edge/S/telemetry.
expected: SCOPES says sites:read is 'Read its site's settings (no money fields)' and plans:read is 'Read its site's current plan' (apikeys.py:35-39). The current plan at /plan should need plans:read, and sites:read should cover the site's settings, not all its data. Plan Part 10.5 names two key kinds, which should differ in what they may hold (for example, only edge keys write telemetry).
actual: RESOURCES (apikeys.py:42-43) maps ^/api/sites/[^/]+/plans(/|$) to plans and every other /api/sites/{id}/... path to sites. So /plan (routes_plans.py:21) is a sites:read path, and plans:read gates only the history and the signed message. apikeys.fields accepts any kind with any scope (apikeys.py:97-115); kind is stored and never read.
evidence: apikeys.py:35-43, 79-84; api.py:266-274 (scope check); routes_plans.py:21 vs 63/69.

title: Lowest role can drive unbounded disk and CPU work: unlimited synchronous report generation, and costly GETs throttled only at 6000 a minute
label: bug
steps:
As the viewer, loop POST /api/reports {"kind":"energy_only","site_id":S,"period":"2026-11"}. Each call runs ReportLab inside the request and writes a new PDF and CSV under data/reports/<company>/ (reports.py:174-183). Nothing caps or prunes them; the listing shows only the newest 200 (reports.py:209). The per-user limit is 6000 a minute (auth.py:79).
Also, GET /api/sites/{id}/plan/compare (routes_plans.py:106-128) runs two 2,880-minute twin simulations per call, with no permission and no cache.
expected: Plan Part 10.6: reports run in the job pool (202 plus polling) with a request-hash cache. Expected: a per-company cap or retention for report files, de-duplication of identical (kind, site, period) requests, and tighter limits on expensive routes. HANDOFF 8.A.3 and trap 1 record that plan quality degrades under CPU load, so a viewer looping these routes worsens every company's plans.
actual: A viewer can fill the disk and load the CPU of the single API process. The rate limits are documented as only 'stopping a script' (auth.py:74-80).
evidence: routes_reports.py:29-39; reports.py:75-185 (no cap, no de-duplication); auth.py:79 (RATE_LIMITS user 6000/60 s); routes_plans.py:106-128.

title: Sign-out ends only the refresh token: the access token keeps working for up to an hour after logout
label: bug
steps:
1) POST /api/local/session to get an access_token and a refresh_token.
2) POST /api/local/logout {"refresh_token":...} returns {signed_out:true}.
3) GET /api/fleet with Authorization: Bearer <same access_token> still returns 200 until exp (ACCESS_MINUTES = 60).
expected: The docstring says 'the session of that token ends' (routes_local.py:7, 117). The access token should be refused after logout: for example, record the session_id from the JWT on logout and check it in companies._local_context, or let logout move a per-session cutoff, as set_password does with sessions_from.
actual: platform.end_session revokes only the refresh-token family (platform.py:521-527). signed_in() checks iat only against sessions_from, which is set by a password change or disable (platform.py:336-344). A token captured before logout stays valid for up to 60 minutes.
evidence: routes_local.py:116-122; platform.py:521-533; companies.py:221-226.

title: Password lockout counts per (email, address) only; behind an untrusted proxy every client shares the 'forwarded' bucket
label: bug
steps:
(a) From N addresses, each address may try 5 passwords per 15 minutes for one account (lock_wait with an address, platform.py:564-578). There is no account-wide cap, unlike the founder's code step (CODE_TRIES across all addresses).
(b) Deploy behind nginx or Caddy without GRIDLYTICS_TRUST_PROXY=1. Every request carries X-Forwarded-For, so client_address() returns 'forwarded' for everyone (platform.py:543-544). Five wrong passwords for victim@x from anywhere then lock victim@x for all users for 15 minutes, and the guard's address limiter buckets everyone under the proxy's IP.
expected: An account-wide soft cap (NIST SP 800-63B 5.2.2), and a start-up refusal or loud warning when forwarded headers arrive without TRUST_PROXY on a non-loopback host. DEPLOY.md is not yet written (DEP items open).
actual: Distributed guessing is limited only by the per-address counts. A proxy deployment that misses one setting turns the lockout into a targeted denial of service.
evidence: platform.py:538-545, 564-578; local_session (routes_local.py:86-97) calls _locked(email, address).

title: Per-site Ed25519 signing key is written with default permissions and only then chmod-ed to 0600
label: bug
steps: On the first plan of a new site, delivery._site_key writes the PKCS8 private key with path.write_bytes(...) (default umask, typically 0644) and then calls os.chmod(path, 0o600) (lines 262-266). Between the two calls, and permanently if chmod fails (the OSError is swallowed), another local user can read the plan-signing key and forge plans the edge accepts.
expected: Create the file atomically with os.open(path, O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL, 0o600), as seed_demo.py:116-118 and identity._kept_secret (identity.py:168) already do. Plan Part 2.8: 'private keys in 0600 files'.
actual: The file is written first and its mode narrowed afterwards; a chmod failure is ignored.
evidence: delivery.py:262-266 vs seed_demo.py:116-119 and identity.py:166-173.

title: Founder session secret has no minimum length; a short GRIDLYTICS_FOUNDER_SESSION_SECRET makes founder tokens forgeable offline
label: bug
steps: Set GRIDLYTICS_FOUNDER_SESSION_SECRET=abc (with the other three settings valid) and start the API. need_set_up() passes. One founder token (base64url payload plus HMAC-SHA256) then lets an attacker brute-force the 3-character secret offline and mint {"sub":"founder","exp":...} tokens for the whole console.
expected: Refuse a session secret under 32 characters in need_set_up() or at start-up, as identity.check_startup does for GRIDLYTICS_LOCAL_JWT_SECRET (identity.py:121-125, SECRET_CHARS = 32).
actual: missing() checks only presence and malformed() checks only the TOTP secret and the password hash (founder.py:93-119). The seed makes a strong secret (seed_demo.py:291, token_urlsafe(48)), but a hand-set one is not checked.

title: POST /control/{action} parses hours and soc_pct with bare float() before the permission check: any member can trigger a 500

actual: An unhandled exception produces a 500 and an error log line from the lowest role.
evidence: routes_plans.py:151-161; api.py:315-321 (unanswered request leads to a 500).

title: Switchback .ics injects the site name unescaped: a name containing CRLF adds arbitrary iCalendar properties or events
label: bug

BEGIN:VALARM

END:VALARM"}. SiteFields.name is any string of up to 120 characters, so CR and LF are allowed (sites.py:49).

title: The demo build lock is process-wide: one company's demo build blocks another company's and tells it a demo is 'already being built'

title: The 12 site pages never set document.title, and focus is not managed on route change
label: bug

2. Click a site, then Plan, Telemetry and so on: the tab still reads 'Fleet · Gridlytics'.

PageHeader is used only by fleet, alerts, reports, tariffs, company-settings, account, new-site and the founder pages. title: Recharts 3 makes each chart a focusable role=application inside a role=img wrapper: unnamed tab stops, one per Fleet row
label: bug
steps:
1. Open /fleet with sites that have a 7-day saving.
2. Tab through the Sites table: after each row's links and stamps comes an extra stop on the sparkline's <svg>.
3. Do the same on Battery (Daily cycles), Genset (Fuel curve) and Savings (daily chart).
expected: Charts wrapped as a static role=img are not focusable; pass accessibilityLayer={false} (or tabIndex={-1}) to BarChart/LineChart. Otherwise expose the recharts keyboard layer with a proper name and without the role=img wrapper.
actual:
Recharts 3.10.1 defaults accessibilityLayer to true (node_modules/recharts/es6/chart/CartesianChart.js:24). RootSurface then sets tabIndex=0 and role="application" on the <svg> (es6/container/RootSurface.js:40-51). The app wraps each chart in <span|div role="img" aria-label>:
- spark-bars.tsx:10
- battery-charts.tsx:49
- genset-cards.tsx:23
- daily-savings-chart.tsx:16
That is a focusable control nested inside an element whose children are presentational (axe 'nested-interactive'). The svg gets no accessible name and captures arrow keys. On Fleet this adds one such stop per site row.
evidence: grep -rn accessibilityLayer src returns nothing (no override). RootSurface.js: `tabIndex = hasAccessibilityLayer ? 0 : undefined; ... role = hasAccessibilityLayer ? 'application' : undefined`.

title: Selects that write or reload on every change: arrow keys on Windows switch company, change member roles and suspend memberships
label: bug
steps:
On Windows (Chrome, Edge or Firefox, where ArrowUp/Down on a closed <select> changes the value and fires change), as an administrator:

2. Sidebar 'Company' select (a person in two or more companies): press ArrowDown.
3. Founder console > Users: on a membership's 'Company role' select press ArrowUp, or on 'Membership' press ArrowDown.
4. Outages log: arrow on a 'Cause' select.
expected: Changing a select only stages the value. Either an explicit Save/Apply button commits it, or a confirmation is asked for role, ownership and status changes. Focus stays on the control.
actual:
- Members (members-tab.tsx:101-102): the first arrow press immediately PATCHes the member to the adjacent role, e.g. Operator -> Administrator, a privilege escalation never confirmed. The select is then disabled while pending (busy(m), line 72), so focus drops and the intended role cannot be reached.

The onChange handlers call mutate/act/setCurrentCompanyId directly:
- members-tab.tsx:102 `onChange={(e) => change.mutate({ m, body: { role: ... } })}`
- company-switch.tsx:23 `onChange={(e) => ... setCurrentCompanyId(e.target.value)}`
- founder-users.tsx:65 and :69 `onChange={(e) => { ... void act(...updateMembership...) }}`
ROLES order is admin, operator, analyst, viewer (members-tab.tsx:28); COMPANY_ROLE_WORDS is owner, admin, member (ops/forms.ts:10).

title: Lettered wizards drop keyboard focus to <body> on Next, Previous and Edit, and never move it to the new step

title: Unmetered genset fuel shows as an 'estimated' 0.0 L on Overview, and as 0 L on Savings for ranges over 62 days
label: bug

The backend /now sums the day rows' litres (routes_sites.py:419, `(d.get(k) or 0)`), and telemetry.aggregate_day stores litres from filled(), which turns blank fuel into 0 (telemetry.py:420, :516). 3) Or open Savings with a custom period longer than 62 days: routes_savings.py:25-37 keeps the metered sum, with blanks counted as 0 and litres_source null.
expected: DESIGN_LOG round 1/2 says unmetered genset fuel is unknown ('genset_unknown, litres null'), never zero. Plan 9.7 says 'Estimated' goes on curve-derived litres only. The Overview tile should say 'not metered', or show curve litres marked Estimated; metered litres (the Faisalabad flow meter, the farm's tank level) should not be called estimated.
actual: The 'Genset this month' tile reads e.g. '42.0 h' with the sub-line '0.0 L (estimated)'.
