evidence: overview-page.tsx:193 `sub={`${litres(n.month.litres)} (estimated)`}`. The /now answer carries no estimated or litres_source flag. telemetry.filled() runs nan_to_num on 'fuel'.

title: Multi-day charts label the time axis with HH:MM only (every day tick reads '00:00'), with ticks placed in the browser's own zone
label: ux
steps: 1) Telemetry, choose '7 days' or '30 days' (telemetry-pickers.tsx; the API returns 15-minute or hourly points). 2) Look at the x-axis. 3) Battery's SoC chart (96 h) and the Overview chart (48 h) do the same. 4) Repeat in a browser set to UTC or Asia/Kolkata.
expected: Plan 9.7 asks for Karachi times whatever the browser's zone, and the telemetry explorer should cover 'any series over any range'. A multi-day axis should show the Karachi date at day ticks (e.g. 'Fri 6 Nov'), with ticks at Karachi midnights.
actual: The axisLabel formatter is always pktTime() (HH:MM), so day-level ticks all read '00:00' (or '05:00' in a UTC browser) and the reader cannot tell which day a feature falls on without hovering. ECharts computes 'nice' tick positions in local time unless useUTC is set (node_modules/echarts/lib/scale/Time.js:57 'local time by default'), so in a browser outside PKT the ticks fall on odd Karachi hours and day boundaries are off. The same formatter is in plan-gantt.tsx:105 and fan-chart.tsx:87.
evidence: time-series-chart.tsx:83 `axisLabel: { formatter: (v) => pktTime(Math.floor(v / 1000)) }`. No useUTC anywhere in components/charts. The tooltip header is right (axisPointer label formatter uses pktDateTime).

title: The chain runs through non-claiming arm periods (monitor tier, not_applied) into the first claiming day, valuing a start gap at v_end, which the PR rejects at switchback boundaries

The start gap is the drift between the twin's native replay and the real battery, which actually ran native during monitoring. It is credited or debited at v_end in a claim, while what native realises from it lands in the cost levers. 4) For a native-to-plan switchback boundary the PR restarts from the measured state, because v_end over-values a handed-over gap (DESIGN_LOG round 6: Faisalabad 3,263 credited against 1,771 realised). Otherwise record in DESIGN_LOG why an activation is different from a switchback block start. Chaining through days withheld for data reasons (battery or genset blank) is fine.
actual: Activation and not-applied gaps chain through, so the first claim of an active period carries a v_end-valued start gap that was built while the plan was not in control.
evidence: verify.py:683-692 (restart only for switch, no row, no_state, or non-claiming with unread_min>0); DESIGN_LOG.md:26-28 ('A day that claims nothing on fully read inputs keeps the chain: a monitor site, a table not applied...'); DESIGN_LOG.md:41-51 (switchback rationale for restarting); test_fix_r6_savings.py:315-330.

evidence: API (owner): /api/sites/e9941b41c70b/now gives month.saving_rs 1956.0; /api/sites/e9941b41c70b/savings gives baselines.native.saving_rs 43593.81, claimed_rs 43593.81, levers.mdi 41637.5, and its days sum to 1956.31. title: Headline savings rest on carry-over credit: Faisalabad's whole saving is carry-over on a day its actual cost was higher than native
label: bug

actual: Faisalabad: 'Saving against the native settings Rs 1,901 — Claimed on verified days: Rs 1,901'. The ledger is: Off-peak energy -Rs 4,149, Battery wear Rs 1,666, Carry-over Rs 4,383, giving Rs 1,901. On the only confirmed day (8 Nov) the Days table shows Actual cost Rs 47,391 against Native cost Rs 44,908, so the plan cost Rs 2,483 more and the whole claim is the value put on the energy left in the battery. That battery is then held at 95 % for days ('Hold for outage'). Rahim Yar Khan: Rs 12,581 claimed, of which carry-over is Rs 9,244 (73 %), while 'Diesel saved -0.3 L' shows the plan burnt more diesel than native. The fee check is built on these claims too (Verified saving a month Rs 1,719 and Rs 47,178).
evidence: API /api/sites/6d4db49bf87e/savings, day 2026-11-08: actual_cost_rs 47390.56, native_cost_rs 44907.88, levers {offpeak_energy -4148.59, wear 1665.9, carry_over 4383.82}, saving_native_rs 1901.13, fidelity 'confirmed'. RYK baselines.native.levers.carry_over 9244, litres_saved -0.3. docs/DESIGN_LOG.md:24-30 records 'Open: the per-day carry-over at off-grid sites is noisy … Customers see the per-day ledger, so this matters before a pilot'. title: Battery uncertainty never re-anchors at soc_max 95 %, so σ climbs to its 15 % cap and the reserve keeps the mill's battery full through every peak
label: bug
steps:
1) GET /api/sites/6d4db49bf87e/battery: sigma_pct 13.0, max SoC in the cycles list 95.0.
2) GET /api/sites/6d4db49bf87e/plan: plan fa7d5026e97a; read the hold_for_outage detail at 18:45 and breakdown.discharge_kwh.

actual:
Anchors need est ≥ 0.98, but every demo pack is capped at soc_max 0.95, so full-charge anchors never happen. σ grows 0.19 points an hour until an outage drains the pack to the low knee.
Implied σ in the reserve (R − Lc·h/η):
- Faisalabad: 0.125–0.15 on 29 Oct–1 Nov
- Lahore: 0.13–0.15 on all 11 days
The 2σ·E widening (up to 30 % of the pack) makes R ≥ the usable band. The current Faisalabad plan therefore holds 95 % for 48 h: Hold 95 % slots all day, discharge 2.17 kWh, 2,090 kWh imported in the peak. Its reserve detail is 184.8 kWh = 128.9 + 55.9 (2 × 0.13 × 215), which is more than the 182.75 kWh usable.
Faisalabad telemetry shows zero peak-window discharge on every plan day (28–31 Oct, 8–9 Nov).
The sigma_high alert says 'the plan will ask for a full charge to re-anchor', but the optimiser and plans code has no anchor logic. Rahim Yar Khan sits at σ 25, and its usable_kwh reads 0.0 at 53.5 % SoC.
evidence:
Code:
- battery.py:31: anchors = est >= 0.98 | <= soc_min + 0.02
- battery.py:55: the alert text
- plans.py:256: sigma0 = min(0.15, σ)
- optimise.py:312: R += 2·sig·En
- grep 'anchor' in optimise.py and plans.py: nothing

The recommendation charges 65 kWh from the grid at Rs 39.48 and holds 95 % for 48 h with 0.0 kWh discharge.
In 38 historical plans it recommends grid charging inside the peak window at Rs 48.28; for example ca9949b7aebe charges 18:00–19:00 at 50 kW, 43 kWh in total.
Compare with native: the plan costs Rs 2,701 more than native over the horizon.
